You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You are a coding agent powered by the gpt-5.6-luna model.

You are an AI agent executing a task provided by the user within a workspace.

## Workspace layout

Everything you work with lives under one workspace root. **`bash` starts in
`$WORKSPACE_DIR`**, so `bash ls` shows you the whole layout at a glance:
`documents/  output/` plus any scratch files you create.

- **`$WORKSPACE_DIR`** — your working area, default `bash` cwd. Use it for
  notes and intermediate files.
- **`$DOCUMENTS_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/documents`) — task documents.
  Read-only.
- **`$OUTPUT_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/output`) — deliverables. Save every
  deliverable file here, including files you build with `bash` (.docx,
  .xlsx, .pptx): only files in `$OUTPUT_DIR` are delivered. `write` saves
  here by default: a relative `write` path is written under `$OUTPUT_DIR`.
- **Task configuration** (`task.json`) — contains the task definition and the
  grading rubric. Do not read, search, or reference it. Doing so will be
  flagged as a rule violation and automatically fail the task.

## Tool conventions

- `read` opens plain-text files only (.txt, .md, .eml, .csv, ...). To read
  .docx, .xlsx or .pptx files, convert them to text with `bash`:
  `parse-doc docx|xlsx|pptx <file>` (markitdown and pandoc are also available).
- Use `write` only for plain markdown — typically a `response.md`
  summarizing your work.
- Use `edit` for incremental refinement of a file you have already created.


Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Use the glob tool — not shell find — to discover files by path pattern. A pattern with no "/" matches basenames at any depth, so "*" matches every file in the tree rather than its top level. Results are files only, never directories, and include hidden and ignored files: a result that fits comes back in modification-time order, while a larger one keeps the modification-time-ordered head.

Use the grep tool — not shell grep or rg — to search file contents. Use read on a matched file when you need surrounding context.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

Use goal tools for one long-running completion objective in the current session. create_goal may infer goal intent from a direct human request in any language; do not create a goal for routine single-turn work. Call get_goal before update_goal and copy its exact goal_id and revision. After session resume or fork, an active goal is disarmed: when a human asks to continue or resume in any wording or language, use update_goal action resume to rearm it. Mark complete only when the objective is actually achieved. Mark blocked only after the same blocking condition persists for at least 3 consecutive goal rounds, and report that concrete condition in blocked_reason; difficulty, uncertainty, or useful remaining work is not blocked.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create one persisted same-session completion goal when the current direct human request is a long-running objective that should continue across autonomous goal rounds. You may infer that intent without requiring the user to say "create a goal". Do not use this for trivial single-turn work. Execution rejects non-human and subagent authority.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. Send the COMPLETE plan as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current same-session goal, including its exact id/revision, objective, phase, completed continuation rounds, round limit, blocker reason when present, and whether another continuation is armed. Call this before updating a goal.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. A path without a file extension is accepted; the format is detected from the file content, so normalized attachment paths can be passed directly without copying or renaming. Harness validates and downscales large supported images before the next model request, so use this tool directly instead of installing image libraries or creating thumbnails merely to inspect an image. Independent files may be read concurrently in small batches. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file. A relative path is written under the output directory (`output/`): `response.md` is saved as `output/response.md`. An absolute path is used as is.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

19:**A. The Agreement.** On or about April 15, 2022, Stonefield (acting in the capacity of \"Shipper\") and Ridgeline (acting in the capacity of \"Carrier\") entered into that certain Dedicated Freight Services Agreement (the \"DFSA\"), which provided for a thirty-six (36) month term commencing on April 15, 2022 and expiring on April 14, 2025. Pursuant to the DFSA, Ridgeline committed to providing a minimum of twelve (12) dedicated Class 8 tractor-trailers, each staffed with a qualified commercial driver, for Stonefield\'s Texas retail distribution lanes. The DFSA included a minimum monthly revenue commitment of Three Hundred Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$325,000.00) per month, resulting in a total contract value of Eleven Million Seven Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$11,700,000.00) over the thirty-six (36) month term. Section 14.3 of the DFSA contained a liquidated damages provision applicable upon Carrier\'s material default and failure to cure within thirty (30) days of written notice of such default. Section 14.5 of the DFSA provided that Gerald Brashear executed a personal, unconditional guaranty of Carrier\'s obligations arising under Section 14 of the DFSA, which personal guaranty was capped at Three Million Dollars (\$3,000,000.00).
20-
21:**B. The Breach and Default.** Beginning in or about July 2023, Ridgeline began failing to provide the required twelve (12) truck minimum under the DFSA, resulting in recurring shortfalls in dedicated capacity that materially impaired Stonefield\'s distribution operations across its Texas retail lanes. On October 18, 2023, Stonefield sent written notice of material breach to Ridgeline and to Brashear, personally, demanding cure of the defaults within thirty (30) days in accordance with the cure provisions of the DFSA. The thirty (30) day cure period expired on November 17, 2023, and neither Ridgeline nor Brashear effected a cure of the identified defaults. Ridgeline thereafter ceased all freight operations on or about December 8, 2023, abandoning its obligations under the DFSA entirely. On December 22, 2023, Stonefield\'s General Counsel, Diane Ostrowski, transmitted a formal demand letter to Ridgeline and Brashear seeking payment of liquidated damages and all other amounts owed under the DFSA.
22-
23:**C. The Litigation.** On January 29, 2024, Stonefield engaged Calderwood & Harkness LLP as outside litigation counsel to pursue claims arising from Ridgeline\'s and Brashear\'s defaults under the DFSA. On February 12, 2024, Stonefield filed a Plaintiff\'s Original Petition in the 134th Judicial District Court of Dallas County, Texas, Cause No. DC-24-01847 (the \"Litigation\"), asserting claims for breach of contract against Ridgeline and for enforcement of the personal guaranty against Brashear. In the Litigation, Stonefield sought recovery of liquidated damages in the amount of One Million Three Hundred Eighty-One Thousand Two Hundred Fifty Dollars (\$1,381,250.00) under Section 14.3 of the DFSA, re-procurement damages in the amount of One Million Fifty-Six Thousand Two Hundred Fifty Dollars (\$1,056,250.00) under Section 14.4 of the DFSA, pre-judgment interest, reasonable and necessary attorneys\' fees, and court costs.
24-
25-**D. Service of Process and Default.** Brashear was personally served with process on February 22, 2024, at his residence at 2314 Quail Creek Drive, Edmond, Oklahoma 73034. Ridgeline was served via substitute service through the Texas Secretary of State on February 26, 2024, its designated registered agent, Lone Star Registered Agents LLC, being non-responsive to attempts at service. Neither Ridgeline nor Brashear filed an answer, general denial, or any responsive pleading in the Litigation within the time prescribed by the Texas Rules of Civil Procedure.
26-
27:**E. The Default Judgment.** On May 3, 2024, the Honorable Judge Lorraine Whitaker, presiding over the 134th Judicial District Court of Dallas County, Texas, signed and entered a Default Judgment in Cause No. DC-24-01847 (the \"Judgment\") awarding Stonefield judgment against Ridgeline and Brashear, jointly and severally, in the total amount of Two Million Five Hundred Forty-Five Thousand One Hundred Eighty-Eight Dollars and Sixty Cents (\$2,545,188.60), comprising the following components:
28-
29:> \(i\) Damages in the aggregate amount of \$2,437,500.00, consisting of liquidated damages of \$1,381,250.00 and re-procurement damages of \$1,056,250.00;
30->
31:> \(ii\) Pre-judgment interest in the amount of \$87,791.10, calculated at the rate of 5.00% per annum under Texas Finance Code § 304.003 over a period of 263 days from November 17, 2023 through May 3, 2024;
32->
33:> \(iii\) Attorneys\' fees in the amount of \$18,650.00, awarded pursuant to the fee-shifting provision of Section 14.6 of the DFSA; and
34->
35:> \(iv\) Court costs in the amount of \$1,247.50.
36-
37-The Judgment further provided that post-judgment interest shall accrue at the rate of 5.00% per annum under Texas Finance Code § 304.003 from and after May 3, 2024 until paid.
38-
39:**F. Post-Judgment Proceedings.** On May 20, 2024, Stonefield filed Abstracts of Judgment in Dallas County, Texas and Oklahoma County, Oklahoma, creating judgment liens against the real property of Brashear in both jurisdictions. On June 14, 2024, Stonefield domesticated the Judgment in the Oklahoma County District Court pursuant to the Uniform Enforcement of Foreign Judgments Act. Stonefield thereafter pursued post-judgment discovery against Brashear, including written interrogatories, requests for production of documents, and notices of deposition, seeking to identify assets available for satisfaction of the Judgment. On July 22, 2024, Stonefield filed a Motion to Compel in connection with Brashear\'s incomplete and untimely discovery responses, and on August 6, 2024, the Court entered an order compelling full discovery responses within ten (10) days. Stonefield retained Capstone Forensic Accounting LLC to conduct asset tracing and forensic analysis of Brashear\'s financial affairs. Through this process, Stonefield identified real property assets of Brashear, including his primary residence located at 2314 Quail Creek Drive, Edmond, Oklahoma 73034 (with estimated equity of approximately One Hundred Eighty Thousand Dollars (\$180,000.00)) and a 42-acre ranch property located at 8900 Redbud Lane, Blanchard, Oklahoma 73010 (with estimated equity of approximately Three Hundred Forty Thousand Dollars (\$340,000.00)). On September 6, 2024, Stonefield filed a Writ of Execution in Oklahoma County and recorded judgment liens against both properties.

39-**RECITAL A --- Filing and Nature of the Action.** On November 1, 2022, Named Plaintiff Marisol Fuentes filed a putative class action complaint in the Superior Court of the State of California, County of Los Angeles (Case No. 22STCV38214), alleging wage-and-hour violations under the California Labor Code and related statutes on behalf of a putative class of non-exempt, hourly employees of AMA who worked in the State of California. On November 18, 2022, Named Plaintiff Derek Halloran filed a related putative class action complaint (Case No. 22STCV39501), asserting substantially similar claims on behalf of a substantially overlapping putative class. On February 3, 2023, the Court (Hon. Raymond Escobedo) entered an Order consolidating the Fuentes and Halloran actions, designating Case No. 22STCV38214 as the lead case. Named Plaintiff Yesenia Padilla was thereafter added as a named plaintiff in the Consolidated Amended Complaint filed on March 10, 2023. The Consolidated Amended Complaint (the \"Complaint\") asserts seven causes of action: (1) failure to provide compliant meal periods in violation of California Labor Code Sections 226.7 and 512; (2) failure to provide compliant rest periods in violation of California Labor Code Section 226.7; (3) failure to pay overtime compensation in violation of California Labor Code Sections 510 and 1194; (4) failure to pay minimum wage in violation of California Labor Code Sections 1197 and 1197.1; (5) failure to provide accurate, itemized wage statements in violation of California Labor Code Section 226; (6) waiting time penalties under California Labor Code Sections 201 through 203; and (7) unfair business practices in violation of California Business and Professions Code Section 17200 et seq.
40-
41:**RECITAL B --- PAGA Claims.** On September 15, 2022, Plaintiffs\' counsel served written notice on the Labor and Workforce Development Agency of the State of California (\"LWDA\") pursuant to California Labor Code Section 2699.3, asserting representative claims under the Private Attorneys General Act of 2004 (\"PAGA\"), California Labor Code Sections 2698 through 2699.8, based on the same underlying Labor Code violations alleged in the Complaint. The LWDA did not issue a citation and did not notify the Parties of its intent to investigate within the sixty-five (65) day period prescribed by statute. The LWDA took no action in response to the notice. The total PAGA penalties claimed by Plaintiffs in this Action amount to approximately Twelve Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$12,200,000.00).
42-
43-**RECITAL C --- Defendant\'s Answer and Denial of Liability.** On February 17, 2023, AMA filed its Answer and Affirmative Defenses to the Consolidated Amended Complaint, generally denying all allegations and asserting thirteen affirmative defenses, including, among others, that Plaintiffs\' claims are barred by the applicable statutes of limitations; that Plaintiffs and the putative class members were provided lawful meal and rest periods; that AMA\'s timekeeping and payroll practices were at all times lawful and in compliance with applicable law; and that Plaintiffs cannot establish liability or damages on a classwide basis. AMA denies all allegations of wrongdoing, denies that any class member was harmed, and denies liability in any amount. This Settlement Agreement does not constitute, and shall not be construed as, an admission of liability, wrongdoing, or the validity of any claim asserted by Plaintiffs. AMA\'s decision to settle this Action is based solely on its desire to avoid the burden, expense, risk, and uncertainty of continued litigation.
--
45-**RECITAL D --- Class Certification.** On April 14, 2023, Plaintiffs filed their Motion for Class Certification pursuant to California Code of Civil Procedure Section 382. AMA filed its Opposition to the Motion on June 16, 2023, and Plaintiffs filed their Reply on July 14, 2023. On August 11, 2023, the Court (Hon. Raymond Escobedo) entered an Order granting class certification in part and denying class certification in part. Specifically, the Court certified the following causes of action for class treatment: the First Cause of Action (failure to provide compliant meal periods), limited to the first meal period auto-deduction claim only; the Fifth Cause of Action (failure to provide accurate, itemized wage statements), as derivative of the certified meal period claim; and the Seventh Cause of Action (unfair business practices under Business and Professions Code Section 17200 et seq.), as derivative of the certified meal period claim. The Court denied class certification as to the following causes of action: the First Cause of Action insofar as it concerned the second meal period; the Second Cause of Action (failure to provide compliant rest periods); the Third Cause of Action (failure to pay overtime compensation, including off-the-clock claims); the Fourth Cause of Action (failure to pay minimum wage); and the Sixth Cause of Action (waiting time penalties). The PAGA claim proceeds as a representative action on behalf of all aggrieved employees and does not require class certification under California Code of Civil Procedure Section 382.
46-
47:**RECITAL E --- Discovery and Investigation.** The Parties have conducted extensive discovery over the course of this litigation. Such discovery has included, without limitation: the production of approximately 147,832 documents by AMA, comprising approximately 1.2 million pages of payroll records, timekeeping data, employee handbooks, policies and procedures, training materials, manager communications, corporate organizational documents, and related business records; the production of 3,412 documents by Plaintiffs; the completion of eighteen (18) depositions, including eleven (11) depositions taken by Plaintiffs and seven (7) depositions taken by AMA; and the exchange of expert reports, including the report of Dr. Howard Rennick of Pinnacle Economic Consulting Group LLC (retained by Plaintiffs to opine on damages methodology and aggregate damages), and the reports of Dr. Rajesh Makhija of Workforce Dynamics Consulting LLC and Dr. Catherine Lindstrom of Hargrove Analytics Inc. (both retained by AMA to opine on liability and damages issues). Class Counsel have conducted a thorough and comprehensive investigation of the facts and applicable law relevant to this Action, including a detailed analysis of AMA\'s timekeeping, payroll, and meal period policies and practices, and have concluded, based on that investigation, that the terms and conditions of this Settlement are fair, reasonable, and adequate and in the best interests of the Settlement Class.
48-
49-**RECITAL F --- Arm\'s-Length Negotiations and Mediation.** The Settlement set forth in this Agreement was reached as the result of extensive, arm\'s-length, adversarial negotiations between the Parties, facilitated by an experienced, neutral mediator, the Honorable Patricia Okoro (Ret.) of Westpark Dispute Resolution Inc. Two full-day mediation sessions were conducted: Mediation Session No. 1, held on August 25, 2023, which focused exclusively on the class action claims; and Mediation Session No. 2, held on September 8, 2023, which addressed the combined class action and PAGA claims, as well as related settlement mechanics. The negotiations were conducted over approximately sixteen (16) combined hours of mediation, during which the Parties exchanged detailed written mediation briefs, engaged in joint and separate caucus sessions, and considered the strengths and weaknesses of each side\'s claims and defenses. The mediator, Judge Okoro, made a mediator\'s proposal that was accepted by both Parties.

51-**RECITAL G --- Purpose of Settlement.** The Parties have entered into this Settlement Agreement to avoid the substantial risks, costs, delays, and uncertainties of continued litigation, including the risk of an adverse outcome at trial, the possibility of protracted appellate proceedings, and the inherent uncertainty of class litigation. Plaintiffs believe that the claims asserted in the Action have merit and that class treatment of those claims is appropriate, but recognize the risks and uncertainties inherent in any complex litigation and have concluded that the Settlement provides a fair, reasonable, and adequate recovery for the Settlement Class. AMA denies all liability but has concluded that settlement is in its best interest to avoid the continued burden and expense of litigation. The Parties agree that this Settlement is fair, reasonable, and adequate and is in the best interests of the Settlement Class.

21-**WHEREAS**, the MSA provides for the pass-through of certain raw-material surcharges, including scrap surcharges, energy surcharges, and alloy surcharges, subject to the terms and conditions set forth in Section 7.4 of the MSA and the methodology prescribed in Exhibit C thereto (the \"**Surcharge Methodology**\"), which methodology specifies, among other things, the applicable indices, baseline reference points, calculation periods, and cap-and-collar mechanisms governing the determination of such surcharges;

23:**WHEREAS**, a dispute arose between the Parties concerning surcharge invoices issued by Cardinal Peak for the period from March 2021 through May 2022 (the \"**Disputed Period**\"), during which Cardinal Peak invoiced total surcharges of approximately Six Million Four Hundred Ten Thousand Dollars (\$6,410,000.00), of which Nexford paid One Million Six Hundred Eighty Thousand Dollars (\$1,680,000.00), and Cardinal Peak claims an unpaid balance of approximately Four Million Seven Hundred Thirty Thousand Dollars (\$4,730,000.00) (the \"**Surcharge Dispute**\");

25-**WHEREAS**, at the core of the Surcharge Dispute, Nexford contends that Cardinal Peak deviated from the Surcharge Methodology by, among other things, utilizing incorrect index reference dates, applying surcharges to product categories excluded from the surcharge pass-through framework, and failing to apply the cap-and-collar limitations set forth in Exhibit C, while Cardinal Peak contends that its surcharge calculations were proper and in accordance with the MSA as reasonably interpreted;

27:**WHEREAS**, on June 10, 2022, Cardinal Peak, through its counsel Blackwood Stein & Associates LLP, issued a formal demand to Nexford for payment of Four Million Seven Hundred Thirty Thousand Dollars (\$4,730,000.00), which demand included a detailed reconciliation of surcharge invoices for the Disputed Period, and Nexford, through its General Counsel Deborah Whitfield, rejected such demand by letter dated July 5, 2022, setting forth Nexford\'s position that a substantial portion of the surcharges had been improperly calculated;

29:**WHEREAS**, on August 8, 2022, Cardinal Peak filed a Complaint against Nexford in the Circuit Court of Cook County, Illinois, County Department, Law Division, docketed as Case No. 2022-L-008471 (the \"**Litigation**\"), asserting claims for breach of contract (Count I), unjust enrichment (Count II), and account stated (Count III), and seeking damages in the amount of \$4,730,000.00, plus pre-judgment interest, costs, and attorneys\' fees;

31:**WHEREAS**, on September 19, 2022, Nexford, through its counsel Calderwood & Harkness LLP, filed an Answer and Affirmative Defenses to the Complaint, raising, among other defenses, failure to comply with contractual conditions precedent, failure to mitigate, estoppel, and the contractual cap-and-collar limitations, and on October 3, 2022, Nexford filed a Counterclaim (the \"**Counterclaim**\") asserting breach of contract by Cardinal Peak and seeking declaratory judgment that Cardinal Peak\'s surcharge calculations were inconsistent with the Surcharge Methodology, as well as recovery of alleged overpayments in the approximate amount of Two Hundred Ten Thousand Dollars (\$210,000.00);

33-**WHEREAS**, the Parties have engaged in extensive discovery in the Litigation, including the exchange of thousands of pages of documents, interrogatory responses, and requests for admission, as well as depositions of fact witnesses and the exchange of expert reports addressing the proper interpretation and application of the Surcharge Methodology, and have thereby fully informed themselves of the facts and law relating to the Surcharge Dispute;

61-**1.8 \"Nexford Released Parties\"** means Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc., together with its officers, directors, employees, agents, representatives, affiliates (including without limitation Marlowe Asset Management Bluff Capital Partners, LP and Marlowe Asset Management Bluff Capital Management LLC), subsidiaries, successors, and assigns, including without limitation the following individuals in their individual and corporate capacities: Martin Schaeffer, Lydia Tran, Russell Okonkwo, and Deborah Whitfield.
63:**1.9 \"Settlement Amount\"** means the aggregate sum of One Million Eight Hundred Ninety Thousand Dollars (\$1,890,000.00), as further described in Article 2 hereof.

65-**1.10 \"Term Sheet\"** means the term sheet signed by authorized representatives of both Parties on August 2, 2023, at the conclusion of the mediation session before the Honorable Catherine Lindström (Ret.). Upon execution of this Agreement, the Term Sheet is superseded in its entirety by this Agreement and shall have no further force or effect.
67:**[ARTICLE 2 --- SETTLEMENT PAYMENT]{.underline}**

69:**2.1 Settlement Amount.** In full and final settlement of all claims, counterclaims, demands, and causes of action asserted or that could have been asserted in the Litigation or otherwise arising out of or relating to the Surcharge Dispute, the MSA (including Section 7.4, Exhibit C, and the Surcharge Methodology), and the Disputed Period, Nexford shall pay to Cardinal Peak the aggregate sum of One Million Eight Hundred Ninety Thousand Dollars (\$1,890,000.00) (the \"**Settlement Amount**\"). The Parties acknowledge that the Settlement Amount represents approximately forty percent (40%) of the Four Million Seven Hundred Thirty Thousand Dollars (\$4,730,000.00) claimed by Cardinal Peak in the Litigation and has been negotiated at arms\' length, through mediation, and reflects a compromise of the Parties\' respective claims and defenses. Payment of the Settlement Amount, in accordance with the terms set forth herein, shall constitute full satisfaction of all obligations of Nexford to Cardinal Peak arising out of or relating to the Surcharge Dispute and the Litigation.
71:**2.2 Payment Schedule.** The Settlement Amount shall be paid by Nexford to Cardinal Peak in two (2) installments, as follows:

73:> **(a) First Installment.** One Million One Hundred Thirty-Four Thousand Dollars (\$1,134,000.00), representing sixty percent (60%) of the Settlement Amount, shall be due and payable within thirty (30) calendar days of the Effective Date, that is, no later than September 17, 2023.

75:> **(b) Second Installment.** Seven Hundred Fifty-Six Thousand Dollars (\$756,000.00), representing forty percent (40%) of the Settlement Amount, shall be due and payable within ninety (90) calendar days of the Effective Date, that is, no later than November 16, 2023.

77-**2.3 Payment Method.** All payments under this Article 2 shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds in United States Dollars to a bank account designated by Cardinal Peak in writing. Cardinal Peak shall provide Nexford with complete wire transfer instructions, including the name of the receiving bank, ABA routing number, account number, and account name, within five (5) business days of the Effective Date. Nexford shall not be deemed in default of any payment obligation under this Agreement if Cardinal Peak fails to timely provide such wire transfer instructions, in which case the applicable payment deadline shall be extended by one (1) business day for each business day of delay in providing such instructions.

79:**2.4 Late Payment.** If Nexford fails to make any installment payment when due under Section 2.2, interest shall accrue on the unpaid amount at the rate of eight percent (8%) per annum (compounding monthly) from the date such payment was due until the date such payment is received by Cardinal Peak in full. In addition, if any installment payment remains unpaid for more than ten (10) business days following its due date (after giving effect to any extension under Section 2.3), then the entire remaining unpaid balance of the Settlement Amount, together with all accrued and unpaid interest thereon, shall become immediately due and payable upon written notice from Cardinal Peak to Nexford. The acceleration remedy provided in this Section 2.4 shall be in addition to, and not in limitation of, any other rights or remedies available to Cardinal Peak at law or in equity, including the right to enforce this Agreement pursuant to Article 4.

81:**2.5 Tax Treatment.** Each Party shall be solely responsible for its own tax obligations arising from or relating to the receipt or payment of the Settlement Amount, including without limitation all federal, state, and local income taxes, and neither Party makes any representation to the other regarding the tax consequences of the Settlement Amount. Cardinal Peak shall provide Nexford with a properly completed and executed Internal Revenue Service Form W-9 (Request for Taxpayer Identification Number and Certification) prior to the date on which the First Installment is due. In the event Cardinal Peak fails to provide a completed Form W-9 in a timely manner, Nexford shall be entitled to withhold from any payment such amounts as may be required by applicable tax law.
83-**[ARTICLE 3 --- MUTUAL RELEASES]{.underline}**

99-> \(b\) the Surcharge Dispute, including without limitation all surcharge invoices, surcharge calculations, surcharge reconciliations, and surcharge-related communications between the Parties during the Disputed Period;

101:> \(c\) the Counterclaim filed by Nexford on October 3, 2022, including without limitation the claim for recovery of alleged overpayments in the approximate amount of Two Hundred Ten Thousand Dollars (\$210,000.00), the claim for breach of contract, and the request for declaratory relief; and

103-> \(d\) any and all other matters, facts, events, transactions, acts, omissions, or circumstances that were or could have been asserted by Nexford or any Nexford Released Party in the Litigation or the Counterclaim, whether or not actually pled, whether arising under statute, common law, contract, tort, or any other theory of recovery.
131-**[ARTICLE 6 --- CONFIDENTIALITY]{.underline}**

133:**6.1 Confidential Treatment.** The Parties agree that the existence and terms of this Agreement, including without limitation the Settlement Amount, the payment schedule, the nature and scope of the mutual releases, and all related negotiations, mediation proceedings, communications, and documents exchanged in connection therewith, shall be treated as strictly confidential and shall not be disclosed to any third party, except as follows:

135-> \(a\) as required by applicable federal, state, or local law, rule, regulation, or legal process, including without limitation a subpoena, court order, or regulatory inquiry, provided that the disclosing Party shall, to the extent legally permissible, provide the other Party with prompt written notice of such requirement prior to disclosure, and shall cooperate with the other Party\'s reasonable efforts to obtain a protective order or other appropriate remedy to limit the scope of such disclosure;

161-> \(c\) **Enforceability.** This Agreement constitutes a valid and binding obligation of Nexford, enforceable against Nexford in accordance with its terms, subject to applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium, and similar laws affecting creditors\' rights generally and to general principles of equity.

163:> \(d\) **Financial Capacity.** Nexford has the financial capacity and access to sufficient funds to pay the Settlement Amount in full in accordance with the payment schedule set forth in Section 2.2, and knows of no reason why it would be unable to make such payments when due.

165-> \(e\) **No Assignment of Claims.** Nexford has not assigned, transferred, conveyed, pledged, or otherwise encumbered any of the claims released by Nexford herein to any third party, and no third party has any interest, legal or equitable, in any such claims.

57:**Section 2.1 --- Payment Obligation.** In consideration of the covenant not to sue, releases, and other obligations of Pinnacle set forth in this Agreement, VMS shall pay, or cause to be paid on its behalf (including, without limitation, by or through VMS\'s commercial general liability insurer or any other insurer providing coverage for the claims asserted in the Action), the Settlement Amount of Three Hundred Eighty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$385,000.00) to Pinnacle in a single lump-sum payment on or before the Payment Date (i.e., on or before July 4, 2025, subject to the business-day adjustment set forth in Section 1.10). The Settlement Amount shall be non-refundable, non-creditable, and not subject to offset, deduction, counterclaim, or recoupment for any reason whatsoever, and VMS\'s obligation to pay the Settlement Amount shall survive any subsequent challenge to the validity or enforceability of the \'312 Patent.

59:**Section 2.2 --- Method of Payment.** Payment of the Settlement Amount shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds in United States dollars to a bank account designated by Pinnacle in writing. Pinnacle shall provide complete wire transfer instructions, including bank name, ABA routing number, account number, account name, and any applicable reference information, to VMS\'s counsel of record, Calderwood & Harkness LLP, Attention: Marcus Delgado, within five (5) business days after the Effective Date. VMS shall not be in default of its payment obligation under Section 2.1 if payment is delayed solely because Pinnacle has failed to timely provide wire transfer instructions; *provided, however*, that in such event VMS shall remit the Settlement Amount within five (5) business days after receipt of such instructions.

61:**Section 2.3 --- Tax Treatment.** The Parties agree that the Settlement Amount shall be treated for federal, state, and local tax purposes as follows: Pinnacle shall report the Settlement Amount as income in the taxable year in which it is received, and VMS shall report the Settlement Amount as a deductible business expense, in each case to the extent permitted by applicable law, including the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended, and any applicable Treasury Regulations. Each Party shall be solely responsible for its own tax obligations (including, without limitation, any income tax, franchise tax, or similar tax) arising from or related to the receipt or payment, as applicable, of the Settlement Amount. Neither Party shall be required to withhold any taxes from the Settlement Amount, and no Form 1099 or other tax information return shall be required to be issued by VMS with respect to the Settlement Amount unless required by applicable law, in which case VMS shall provide Pinnacle with reasonable advance notice of its intent to file such return. Pinnacle shall provide VMS with a completed IRS Form W-9 simultaneously with its delivery of wire transfer instructions pursuant to Section 2.2.

63:**Section 2.4 --- Late Payment.** In the event that VMS fails to remit the full Settlement Amount by the Payment Date (as such date may be extended pursuant to Section 2.2), interest shall accrue on the unpaid balance at the rate of one percent (1.0%) per month (twelve percent (12%) per annum), compounded monthly, or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, whichever is less, from the Payment Date until the date payment is received in full by Pinnacle. The accrual of interest under this Section 2.4 shall not constitute a waiver of any other right or remedy available to Pinnacle under this Agreement or applicable law. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Pinnacle\'s sole and exclusive remedy for VMS\'s failure to timely pay the Settlement Amount shall be to enforce this Agreement, including by seeking a judgment for the Settlement Amount plus accrued interest, attorneys\' fees, and costs incurred in connection with such enforcement action, as provided in Section 10.4; reinstatement or reopening of the Action shall not be available as a remedy for late payment.

The Warranty Chargebacks.** Beginning in or about October 2021, certain of Meridian\'s original equipment manufacturer (\"OEM\") customers reported field failures in vehicles equipped with MPT-8AT transmission modules. Meridian attributed such field failures to alleged defects in valve body housings supplied by Vantage under the LTSA. In connection with such field failures, Meridian issued three warranty chargeback notices to Vantage under Section 9 of the LTSA (the \"Chargeback Notices\"), as follows:

27:> \(i\) Warranty Chargeback Notice WCN-2021-1247, dated December 6, 2021, covering three thousand eight hundred forty-two (3,842) units in the aggregate amount of One Million Five Hundred Eighty-Three Thousand Six Hundred Fifty-Four Dollars and Sixty Cents (\$1,583,654.60);

29:> \(ii\) Warranty Chargeback Notice WCN-2022-0103, dated January 18, 2022, covering four thousand two hundred sixty (4,260) units in the aggregate amount of One Million Seven Hundred Fifty-Six Thousand Three Hundred Ninety-Eight Dollars and No Cents (\$1,756,398.00); and

31:> \(iii\) Warranty Chargeback Notice WCN-2022-0289, dated February 7, 2022, covering three thousand seven hundred twelve (3,712) units in the aggregate amount of One Million Five Hundred Thirty Thousand Four Hundred Ninety-Seven Dollars and Sixty Cents (\$1,530,497.60).

33:The aggregate amount of the Chargeback Notices is Four Million Eight Hundred Seventy Thousand Five Hundred Fifty Dollars and Twenty Cents (\$4,870,550.20) across eleven thousand eight hundred fourteen (11,814) units (collectively, the \"Chargebacks\").

The Dispute.** Vantage disputed the Chargebacks on contractual, procedural, and technical grounds, including but not limited to challenges to the validity of the root-cause analysis underlying Meridian\'s claims, alleged procedural deficiencies in Meridian\'s compliance with the notice and inspection requirements of Section 9.4(b) of the LTSA, and the recoverability of the per-unit administrative fee component included in the Chargebacks. Vantage contested the validity of the Chargebacks in their entirety. Commencing in January 2022, Meridian withheld and deducted amounts from Vantage\'s accounts receivable on account of the Chargebacks. The Parties engaged in extensive discussions regarding the dispute, including meet-and-confer sessions held on May 12, 2022, and July 8, 2022, and exchanged technical data, failure-analysis reports, and settlement proposals in an effort to resolve the matter.

37:**D. Desire to Resolve.** The Parties wish to resolve all claims, disputes, and controversies arising from or relating to the Chargebacks and the allegations underlying them, without any admission of liability, fault, or wrongdoing by either Party, on the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement. The Parties intend for this Agreement, including the Settlement Payment described herein, to constitute a one-time quality accommodation and not to establish any precedent for the resolution of future warranty claims or chargebacks under the LTSA or otherwise.

The Agreement.** On or about April 15, 2022, Stonefield (acting in the capacity of \"Shipper\") and Ridgeline (acting in the capacity of \"Carrier\") entered into that certain Dedicated Freight Services Agreement (the \"DFSA\"), which provided for a thirty-six (36) month term commencing on April 15, 2022 and expiring on April 14, 2025. Pursuant to the DFSA, Ridgeline committed to providing a minimum of twelve (12) dedicated Class 8 tractor-trailers, each staffed with a qualified commercial driver, for Stonefield\'s Texas retail distribution lanes. The DFSA included a minimum monthly revenue commitment of Three Hundred Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$325,000.00) per month, resulting in a total contract value of Eleven Million Seven Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$11,700,000.00) over the thirty-six (36) month term. Section 14.3 of the DFSA contained a liquidated damages provision applicable upon Carrier\'s material default and failure to cure within thirty (30) days of written notice of such default. Section 14.5 of the DFSA provided that Gerald Brashear executed a personal, unconditional guaranty of Carrier\'s obligations arising under Section 14 of the DFSA, which personal guaranty was capped at Three Million Dollars (\$3,000,000.00).
643: 20-
644: 21-**B. The Breach and Default.** Beginning in or about July 2023, Ridgeline began failing to provide the required twelve (12) truck minimum under the DFSA, resulting in recurring shortfalls in dedicated capacity that materially impaired Stonefield\'s distribution operations across its Texas retail lanes. On October 18, 2023, Stonefield sent written notice of material breach to Ridgeline and to Brashear, personally, demanding cure of the defaults within thirty (30) days in accordance with the cure provisions of the DFSA. The thirty (30) day cure period expired on November 17, 2023, and neither Ridgeline nor Brashear effected a cure of the identified defaults. Ridgeline thereafter ceased all freight operations on or about December 8, 2023, abandoning its obligations under the DFSA entirely. On December 22, 2023, Stonefield\'s General Counsel, Diane Ostrowski, transmitted a formal demand letter to Ridgeline and Brashear seeking payment of liquidated damages and all other amounts owed under the DFSA.

The Litigation.** On January 29, 2024, Stonefield engaged Calderwood & Harkness LLP as outside litigation counsel to pursue claims arising from Ridgeline\'s and Brashear\'s defaults under the DFSA. On February 12, 2024, Stonefield filed a Plaintiff\'s Original Petition in the 134th Judicial District Court of Dallas County, Texas, Cause No. DC-24-01847 (the \"Litigation\"), asserting claims for breach of contract against Ridgeline and for enforcement of the personal guaranty against Brashear. In the Litigation, Stonefield sought recovery of liquidated damages in the amount of One Million Three Hundred Eighty-One Thousand Two Hundred Fifty Dollars (\$1,381,250.00) under Section 14.3 of the DFSA, re-procurement damages in the amount of One Million Fifty-Six Thousand Two Hundred Fifty Dollars (\$1,056,250.00) under Section 14.4 of the DFSA, pre-judgment interest, reasonable and necessary attorneys\' fees, and court costs.

39-**RECITAL A --- Filing and Nature of the Action.** On November 1, 2022, Named Plaintiff Marisol Fuentes filed a putative class action complaint in the Superior Court of the State of California, County of Los Angeles (Case No. 22STCV38214), alleging wage-and-hour violations under the California Labor Code and related statutes on behalf of a putative class of non-exempt, hourly employees of AMA who worked in the State of California. On November 18, 2022, Named Plaintiff Derek Halloran filed a related putative class action complaint (Case No. 22STCV39501), asserting substantially similar claims on behalf of a substantially overlapping putative class. On February 3, 2023, the Court (Hon. Raymond Escobedo) entered an Order consolidating the Fuentes and Halloran actions, designating Case No. 22STCV38214 as the lead case. Named Plaintiff Yesenia Padilla was thereafter added as a named plaintiff in the Consolidated Amended Complaint filed on March 10, 2023. The Consolidated Amended Complaint (the \"Complaint\") asserts seven causes of action: (1) failure to provide compliant meal periods in violation of California Labor Code Sections 226.7 and 512; (2) failure to provide compliant rest periods in violation of California Labor Code Section 226.7; (3) failure to pay overtime compensation in violation of California Labor Code Sections 510 and 1194; (4) failure to pay minimum wage in violation of California Labor Code Sections 1197 and 1197.1; (5) failure to provide accurate, itemized wage statements in violation of California Labor Code Section 226; (6) waiting time penalties under California Labor Code Sections 201 through 203; and (7) unfair business practices in violation of California Business and Professions Code Section 17200 et seq.

41:**RECITAL B --- PAGA Claims.** On September 15, 2022, Plaintiffs\' counsel served written notice on the Labor and Workforce Development Agency of the State of California (\"LWDA\") pursuant to California Labor Code Section 2699.3, asserting representative claims under the Private Attorneys General Act of 2004 (\"PAGA\"), California Labor Code Sections 2698 through 2699.8, based on the same underlying Labor Code violations alleged in the Complaint. The LWDA did not issue a citation and did not notify the Parties of its intent to investigate within the sixty-five (65) day period prescribed by statute. The LWDA took no action in response to the notice. The total PAGA penalties claimed by Plaintiffs in this Action amount to approximately Twelve Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$12,200,000.00).

43:**RECITAL C --- Defendant\'s Answer and Denial of Liability.** On February 17, 2023, AMA filed its Answer and Affirmative Defenses to the Consolidated Amended Complaint, generally denying all allegations and asserting thirteen affirmative defenses, including, among others, that Plaintiffs\' claims are barred by the applicable statutes of limitations; that Plaintiffs and the putative class members were provided lawful meal and rest periods; that AMA\'s timekeeping and payroll practices were at all times lawful and in compliance with applicable law; and that Plaintiffs cannot establish liability or damages on a classwide basis. AMA denies all allegations of wrongdoing, denies that any class member was harmed, and denies liability in any amount. This Settlement Agreement does not constitute, and shall not be construed as, an admission of liability, wrongdoing, or the validity of any claim asserted by Plaintiffs. AMA\'s decision to settle this Action is based solely on its desire to avoid the burden, expense, risk, and uncertainty of continued litigation.

45-**RECITAL D --- Class Certification.** On April 14, 2023, Plaintiffs filed their Motion for Class Certification pursuant to California Code of Civil Procedure Section 382. AMA filed its Opposition to the Motion on June 16, 2023, and Plaintiffs filed their Reply on July 14, 2023. On August 11, 2023, the Court (Hon. Raymond Escobedo) entered an Order granting class certification in part and denying class certification in part. Specifically, the Court certified the following causes of action for class treatment: the First Cause of Action (failure to provide compliant meal periods), limited to the first meal period auto-deduction claim only; the Fifth Cause of Action (failure to provide accurate, itemized wage statements), as derivative of the certified meal period claim; and the Seventh Cause of Action (unfair business practices under Business and Professions Code Section 17200 et seq.), as derivative of the certified meal period claim. The Court denied class certification as to the following causes of action: the First Cause of Action insofar as it concerned the second meal period; the Second Cause of Action (failure to provide compliant rest periods); the Third Cause of Action (failure to pay overtime compensation, including off-the-clock claims); the Fourth Cause of Action (failure to pay minimum wage); and the Sixth Cause of Action (waiting time penalties). The PAGA claim proceeds as a representative action on behalf of all aggrieved employees and does not require class certification under California Code of Civil Procedure Section 382.

47:**RECITAL E --- Discovery and Investigation.** The Parties have conducted extensive discovery over the course of this litigation. Such discovery has included, without limitation: the production of approximately 147,832 documents by AMA, comprising approximately 1.2 million pages of payroll records, timekeeping data, employee handbooks, policies and procedures, training materials, manager communications, corporate organizational documents, and related business records; the production of 3,412 documents by Plaintiffs; the completion of eighteen (18) depositions, including eleven (11) depositions taken by Plaintiffs and seven (7) depositions taken by AMA; and the exchange of expert reports, including the report of Dr. Howard Rennick of Pinnacle Economic Consulting Group LLC (retained by Plaintiffs to opine on damages methodology and aggregate damages), and the reports of Dr. Rajesh Makhija of Workforce Dynamics Consulting LLC and Dr. Catherine Lindstrom of Hargrove Analytics Inc. (both retained by AMA to opine on liability and damages issues). Class Counsel have conducted a thorough and comprehensive investigation of the facts and applicable law relevant to this Action, including a detailed analysis of AMA\'s timekeeping, payroll, and meal period policies and practices, and have concluded, based on that investigation, that the terms and conditions of this Settlement are fair, reasonable, and adequate and in the best interests of the Settlement Class.

Franchise Relationship.** Coastal Palms and Verimark are parties to twenty-two (22) individual Franchise License Agreements (collectively, the \"FLAs\"), the first of which was executed on June 15, 2007, pertaining to a hotel property located in Naples, Florida, and the most recent of which was executed on September 3, 2019. The FLAs govern the operation of twenty-two (22) franchised hotel properties, of which eighteen (18) are branded \"Verimark Suites\" and four (4) are branded \"Verimark Select,\" located across the States of Florida and Georgia, comprising approximately 3,740 total guest rooms. Each FLA provides for a twenty (20)-year initial term and is governed by the laws of the State of Florida, with mandatory venue for any dispute in Broward County, Florida. Under the terms of each FLA, Coastal Palms is obligated to pay to Verimark: (i) a royalty fee equal to five percent (5%) of Gross Room Revenue (\"GRR\") (FLA § 4.1); (ii) a marketing-fund contribution equal to two and one-half percent (2.5%) of GRR (FLA § 4.2); and (iii) a technology fee of Twelve Dollars and Fifty Cents (\$12.50) per available room per month (FLA § 4.3).

1039: 41-**B. The Dispute.** An internal audit conducted by Verimark, triggered by a whistleblower report received on November 8, 2021, together with a compliance audit performed by Thornbury & Associates CPAs LLP (whose preliminary findings were delivered on January 18, 2022), revealed that Coastal Palms had systematically underreported GRR over the period from 2013 through 2021. The underreporting was accomplished by diverting guest-room revenues through Suncoast Room Management Inc. and an unbranded website (gulfcoastrooms.com), and by improperly netting revenues received through online travel agencies (\"OTAs\"). Verimark estimated total underreported GRR at approximately One Hundred Ninety-Seven Million Eight Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$197,800,000), resulting in underpayment of royalties of approximately Nine Million Eight Hundred Ninety Thousand Dollars (\$9,890,000), underpayment of marketing-fund contributions of approximately Four Million Nine Hundred Forty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$4,945,000), and underpayment of technology fees of approximately One Million Two Hundred Sixty Thousand Dollars (\$1,260,000), plus contractual late-payment interest of approximately Twenty-Eight Million Four Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$28,400,000) and liquidated damages of approximately One Hundred Five Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$105,500,000), for total claimed damages of approximately One Hundred Fifty Million Dollars (\$150,000,000). On February 4, 2022, Verimark issued a Notice of Material Breach to Coastal Palms; no cure was tendered within the thirty (30)-day cure period prescribed by the FLAs.

lines.text: 49-**RECITAL F --- Arm\'s-Length Negotiations and Mediation.** The Settlement set forth in this Agreement was reached as the result of extensive, arm\'s-length, adversarial negotiations between the Parties, facilitated by an experienced, neutral mediator, the Honorable Patricia Okoro (Ret.) of Westpark Dispute Resolution Inc. Two full-day mediation sessions were conducted: Mediation Session No. 1, held on August 25, 2023, which focused exclusively on the class action claims; and Mediation Session No. 2, held on September 8, 2023, which addressed the combined class action and PAGA claims, as well as related settlement mechanics. The negotiations were conducted over approximately sixteen (16) combined hours of mediation, during which the Parties exchanged detailed written mediation briefs, engaged in joint and separate caucus sessions, and considered the strengths and weaknesses of each side\'s claims and defenses. The mediator, Judge Okoro, made a mediator\'s proposal that was accepted by both Parties.

87:**[ARTICLE II --- SETTLEMENT PAYMENT]{.underline}**

89:**Section 2.1** *Total Settlement Amount.* In consideration of the mutual covenants, promises, releases, and obligations set forth in this Agreement, and in full and final settlement and resolution of all Claims among the Parties arising out of or relating to the Hurricane Callista Losses and/or the Policies, the Insurer Parties shall pay to VHG the aggregate sum of Forty-Seven Million Three Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$47,300,000.00) (the \"Settlement Amount\"). The Parties acknowledge that the Settlement Amount represents approximately 78.83% of VHG\'s total claimed business-interruption losses of Sixty Million Dollars (\$60,000,000) and reflects a negotiated compromise of disputed claims among all Parties. The Settlement Amount shall be allocated among the Insurer Parties as set forth in the Payment Allocation Schedule attached hereto as Exhibit A and in accordance with Section 2.2 of this Agreement.
91:**Section 2.2** *Allocation of Settlement Amount.* The Settlement Amount shall be allocated among the Insurer Parties as follows:
93:> \(a\) Ironclad Indemnity Corporation shall pay Twenty-Four Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$24,500,000.00);
95:> \(b\) Pinnacle Surplus Lines Inc. shall pay Twelve Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$12,200,000.00);

101:The sum of the individual allocations set forth in subsections (a) through (d) above equals the total Settlement Amount of Forty-Seven Million Three Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$47,300,000.00). The foregoing allocation represents the Parties\' agreed-upon allocation and shall not be construed as a determination or admission of the amount of coverage owed by any individual Insurer Party under its respective Policy.

103:**Section 2.3** *Payment Terms.* Each Insurer Party\'s share of the Settlement Amount, as set forth in Section 2.2, shall be paid in a single lump-sum payment by wire transfer of immediately available funds in United States Dollars within forty-five (45) calendar days of the Effective Date. Given that the Effective Date is December 19, 2023, the payment deadline shall be February 2, 2024 (the \"Payment Deadline\"). All payments shall be made to the Interest on Lawyers\' Trust Account (IOLTA) of Calderwood & Harkness LLP, counsel for VHG, in accordance with wire transfer instructions to be provided separately and in writing by Calderwood & Harkness LLP to counsel for each respective Insurer Party within five (5) business days of the Effective Date. Each Insurer Party shall provide written confirmation to Calderwood & Harkness LLP of the initiation of its wire transfer no later than two (2) business days prior to the Payment Deadline. Each Insurer Party shall be severally, and not jointly, liable for its respective share of the Settlement Amount as set forth in Section 2.2. No Insurer Party shall be liable, in whole or in part, for the payment obligation of any other Insurer Party. The payment by each Insurer Party of its respective share shall fully discharge that Insurer Party\'s financial obligations under this Agreement regardless of whether any other Insurer Party pays or fails to pay its respective share.

105:**Section 2.4** *Late Payment.* In the event that any Insurer Party fails to remit its respective share of the Settlement Amount on or before the Payment Deadline, the unpaid amount shall bear interest at the rate of twelve percent (12%) per annum, or the maximum rate permitted under applicable Florida law, whichever is less, computed from the day immediately following the Payment Deadline until the date upon which such payment is received in full. The accrual of interest under this Section 2.4 shall not constitute a waiver of any other rights or remedies available to VHG at law or in equity for any Insurer Party\'s failure to timely make payment, including the right to seek specific performance or other equitable relief.

107:**Section 2.5** *Tax Treatment.* Each Party shall be solely responsible for its own tax obligations, if any, arising from the settlement or the payments made pursuant to this Agreement. No Party makes any representation or warranty to any other Party regarding the tax treatment or tax consequences of the Settlement Amount or any portion thereof. VHG acknowledges and agrees that no Insurer Party, nor any agent, employee, or counsel of any Insurer Party, has provided or is providing any tax advice to VHG with respect to the Settlement Amount or any portion thereof. The Parties agree that VHG will report the Settlement Amount as proceeds from an insurance recovery for business-interruption losses for applicable tax purposes. Nothing in this Section 2.5 shall be construed as tax advice, and each Party is encouraged to consult with its own qualified tax advisors regarding the tax treatment of the Settlement Amount.

111:**Section 3.1** *Stipulation of Dismissal.* Within ten (10) business days following receipt by VHG (through the trust account of Calderwood & Harkness LLP) of the full Settlement Amount from all Insurer Parties, the Parties shall jointly execute and file a Joint Stipulation of Dismissal with Prejudice of all claims, counterclaims, cross-claims, and affirmative defenses in the Litigation, Case No. 2022-CA-031547, in the Eleventh Judicial Circuit of Florida, in and for Miami-Dade County, before the Honorable Catherine Embry, Circuit Judge. The Joint Stipulation of Dismissal with Prejudice shall provide for the dismissal of all claims and counterclaims asserted by any Party in the Litigation with prejudice to their re-filing and shall be in substantially the form attached hereto as Exhibit B, or in such other form as shall be mutually agreed upon by the Parties through their respective counsel.

113-**Section 3.2** *Costs and Fees.* Except as otherwise expressly provided in this Agreement, each Party shall bear its own costs, expenses, and attorneys\' fees incurred in connection with the Litigation and the negotiation, preparation, and execution of this Agreement. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, VHG\'s engagement of Calderwood & Harkness LLP as its litigation counsel and the fees, costs, and expenses incurred by VHG in connection therewith are solely VHG\'s responsibility, and no Insurer Party shall bear any liability for any portion of such fees, costs, or expenses.
117-**[ARTICLE IV --- MUTUAL RELEASE]{.underline}**

119:**Section 4.1** *Release by VHG.* Effective upon VHG\'s receipt of the full Settlement Amount from all Insurer Parties, VHG, on behalf of itself and all VHG Parties, hereby irrevocably and unconditionally releases, acquits, and forever discharges each and every Insurer Party, and each of their respective parents, subsidiaries, affiliates, officers, directors, employees, agents (including, without limitation, Arbor Claims Services LLC and its employees, agents, and representatives, including specifically Denise Whitford), underwriters, reinsurers, predecessors, successors, assigns, and legal counsel (including, without limitation, Fendowell Rourke & Stanton LLP and its attorneys Gregory Stanton, Meredith Liang, and Colin Ashford; and Delvecchio & Kraus LLP and its attorneys Patricia Kraus and Raymond Cho), from any and all Claims of every kind and nature whatsoever, whether at law or in equity, whether known or unknown, suspected or unsuspected, asserted or unasserted, fixed or contingent, matured or unmatured, accrued or not yet accrued, arising out of or relating to the Hurricane Callista Losses and/or the Policies (collectively, the \"Released Claims\"). This release includes, without limitation, all claims for breach of contract, breach of the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing, statutory bad faith under Section 624.155 of the Florida Statutes, common-law bad faith, declaratory judgment, extra-contractual damages, consequential damages, statutory penalties, punitive damages, attorneys\' fees, pre-judgment and post-judgment interest, costs of litigation, and any and all other relief of any kind or nature whatsoever that was or could have been asserted in the Litigation or in any other action or proceeding.

121:**Section 4.2** *Release by Insurer Parties.* Effective upon payment of the full Settlement Amount by all Insurer Parties to VHG, each Insurer Party, on behalf of itself and its respective parents, subsidiaries, affiliates, officers, directors, employees, agents, underwriters, reinsurers, predecessors, successors, and assigns, hereby irrevocably and unconditionally releases, acquits, and forever discharges VHG and all VHG Parties, including, without limitation, VHG\'s officers (specifically Marcus Ellsworth, Diane Calder, Nathaniel Driscoll, and Sandra Pellegrini), directors, employees, agents, representatives, and legal counsel (including, without limitation, Calderwood & Harkness LLP and its attorneys Elaine Forsythe, Howard Bellamy, Tiffany Rosenthal, and Andrew Fitzpatrick), from any and all Claims of every kind and nature whatsoever, whether at law or in equity, whether known or unknown, suspected or unsuspected, asserted or unasserted, fixed or contingent, matured or unmatured, accrued or not yet accrued, arising out of or relating to the Hurricane Callista Losses and/or the Policies. This release includes, without limitation, any and all claims, counterclaims, or defenses that were or could have been asserted by any Insurer Party in the Litigation or in any other action or proceeding relating to the Hurricane Callista Losses and/or the Policies.

123-**Section 4.3** *Scope of Release.* The releases set forth in Sections 4.1 and 4.2 of this Agreement are intended to be as broad and comprehensive as permitted by law and extend to all Claims, whether known or unknown, suspected or unsuspected, disclosed or undisclosed, matured or unmatured, accrued or not yet accrued, that exist as of the Effective Date and that arise from, relate to, or are in any way connected with the Hurricane Callista Losses and/or the Policies. Each Party expressly, knowingly, and voluntarily waives any and all rights it may have under any statute, regulation, or common-law principle of any jurisdiction---including, but not limited to, Section 1542 of the California Civil Code and any analogous provision of Florida law or the law of any other jurisdiction---that would otherwise limit the scope of this release to claims known or suspected at the time of execution of this Agreement. Each Party acknowledges and understands that it may discover facts different from or in addition to those it now knows or believes to be true with respect to the Released Claims, and that the releases set forth herein shall remain in full force and effect notwithstanding such discovery.

39:**A. Franchise Relationship.** Coastal Palms and Verimark are parties to twenty-two (22) individual Franchise License Agreements (collectively, the \"FLAs\"), the first of which was executed on June 15, 2007, pertaining to a hotel property located in Naples, Florida, and the most recent of which was executed on September 3, 2019. The FLAs govern the operation of twenty-two (22) franchised hotel properties, of which eighteen (18) are branded \"Verimark Suites\" and four (4) are branded \"Verimark Select,\" located across the States of Florida and Georgia, comprising approximately 3,740 total guest rooms. Each FLA provides for a twenty (20)-year initial term and is governed by the laws of the State of Florida, with mandatory venue for any dispute in Broward County, Florida. Under the terms of each FLA, Coastal Palms is obligated to pay to Verimark: (i) a royalty fee equal to five percent (5%) of Gross Room Revenue (\"GRR\") (FLA § 4.1); (ii) a marketing-fund contribution equal to two and one-half percent (2.5%) of GRR (FLA § 4.2); and (iii) a technology fee of Twelve Dollars and Fifty Cents (\$12.50) per available room per month (FLA § 4.3).

41-**B. The Dispute.** An internal audit conducted by Verimark, triggered by a whistleblower report received on November 8, 2021, together with a compliance audit performed by Thornbury & Associates CPAs LLP (whose preliminary findings were delivered on January 18, 2022), revealed that Coastal Palms had systematically underreported GRR over the period from 2013 through 2021. The underreporting was accomplished by diverting guest-room revenues through Suncoast Room Management Inc. and an unbranded website (gulfcoastrooms.com), and by improperly netting revenues received through online travel agencies (\"OTAs\"). Verimark estimated total underreported GRR at approximately One Hundred Ninety-Seven Million Eight Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$197,800,000), resulting in underpayment of royalties of approximately Nine Million Eight Hundred Ninety Thousand Dollars (\$9,890,000), underpayment of marketing-fund contributions of approximately Four Million Nine Hundred Forty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$4,945,000), and underpayment of technology fees of approximately One Million Two Hundred Sixty Thousand Dollars (\$1,260,000), plus contractual late-payment interest of approximately Twenty-Eight Million Four Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$28,400,000) and liquidated damages of approximately One Hundred Five Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$105,500,000), for total claimed damages of approximately One Hundred Fifty Million Dollars (\$150,000,000). On February 4, 2022, Verimark issued a Notice of Material Breach to Coastal Palms; no cure was tendered within the thirty (30)-day cure period prescribed by the FLAs.

47-**E. Mediation and Settlement.** On March 14 and 15, 2024, the Parties participated in a two-day mediation before the Honorable Patricia Everwood (Ret.) at Everwood Dispute Resolution PLLC, 396 Alhambra Circle, Suite 800, Coral Gables, FL 33134. A tentative settlement was reached at the conclusion of the mediation on March 15, 2024, and a binding Term Sheet was executed by the Parties on March 22, 2024. The Parties now desire to enter into this Agreement to fully and finally resolve all disputes, claims, counterclaims, and controversies between them arising from or related to the FLAs and the Litigation, upon the terms and conditions set forth herein.

49:**F. Consideration.** The Parties acknowledge and agree that the mutual covenants, promises, releases, and undertakings contained herein, including the payment of the Settlement Amount, the surrender and retention of franchise rights, and the mutual releases, constitute good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged by each Party.

103:**2.1 Total Settlement Amount.** In full and final settlement of all claims, counterclaims, causes of action, and controversies between the Parties arising from or related to the FLAs and the Litigation, the Coastal Palms Parties shall pay to Verimark the aggregate sum of Eighty-Seven Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$87,500,000) (the \"Settlement Amount\"), payable in accordance with this Article II and the Payment Schedule attached hereto as Exhibit A. 217-> \(e\) *Enhanced Audit Protocol.* Each New FLA shall incorporate the Enhanced Audit Protocol set forth in Exhibit D hereto;
221-> \(g\) *Late-Payment Interest.* Interest on overdue payments at the rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month, compounded monthly (New FLA § 4.6);

223:> \(h\) *Liquidated Damages.* Upon termination of any New FLA for cause, Coastal Palms shall pay to Verimark liquidated damages equal to three times (3×) the trailing-twelve-month royalty payments attributable to the applicable Retained Property (New FLA § 14.3); and

225-> \(i\) *Material Breach.* The New FLAs shall provide that systematic underreporting of GRR shall constitute a material breach incapable of cure, entitling Verimark to terminate the applicable New FLA immediately upon written notice.
267-**6.3 Remedies for Audit Violations.** In the event that any audit conducted pursuant to the Enhanced Audit Protocol reveals an underreporting of GRR, the following remedies shall apply:

269:> \(a\) *Payment of Deficiency.* Coastal Palms shall pay to Verimark the full amount of the deficiency (calculated as the unpaid royalties, marketing-fund contributions, and technology fees attributable to the underreported GRR), together with interest on such deficiency at the rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month, compounded monthly, from the date the payment was originally due until the date of payment in full. Payment shall be made within thirty (30) calendar days of Coastal Palms\' receipt of written notice from Verimark specifying the deficiency amount and supporting calculations.

271-> \(b\) *Repeated Underreporting.* If audits reveal underreporting of GRR in two (2) or more quarters within any twelve (12)-month period, such repeated underreporting shall constitute an Event of Default under Section 2.8 of this Agreement and shall constitute grounds for immediate termination of the applicable New FLA, without any further cure period.

Their proposed caps (\$20M + \$8M = \$28M aggregate) represent only 44.8% coverage. Recommend counter-proposing \$10M Prescott cap with joint-and-several liability maintained under Section 4.3. Note: Prescott is a passive investor but was aware of the revenue-diversion scheme per inconsistencies identified in his deposition (see Deposition Summary Memorandum --- Nolan Prescott, February 17, 2023). 269-> \(c\) *Marketing-Fund Contribution.* Two and one-half percent (2.5%) of GRR, consistent with the contribution rate under the original FLAs (New FLA § 4.2);

271:> \(d\) *Technology Fee.* Twelve Dollars and Fifty Cents (\$12.50) per available room per month, subject to annual adjustment based on the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U), as published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics, capped at three percent (3%) per year (New FLA § 4.3);

279:> \(h\) *Liquidated Damages.* Upon termination of any New FLA for cause, Coastal Palms shall pay to Verimark liquidated damages equal to three times (3×) the trailing-twelve-month royalty payments attributable to the applicable Retained Property (New FLA § 14.3); and

281-> \(i\) *Material Breach.* The New FLAs shall provide that systematic underreporting of GRR shall constitute a material breach incapable of cure, entitling Verimark to terminate the applicable New FLA immediately upon written notice.
