335:> \(a\) *Payment of Deficiency.* Coastal Palms shall pay to Verimark the full amount of the deficiency (calculated as the unpaid royalties, marketing-fund contributions, and technology fees attributable to the underreported GRR), together with interest on such deficiency at the rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month, compounded monthly, from the date the payment was originally due until the date of payment in full. 365:**Section 5.1 --- Amount and Duration.** The Husband shall pay to the Wife spousal maintenance in the amount of **Fifteen Thousand Dollars (\$15,000) per month** for a period of **forty-eight (48) months**, commencing on the first day of the first full calendar month following the entry of the Judgment of Divorce. The total spousal maintenance obligation of the Husband under this Agreement is \$720,000 (\$15,000 × 48 months). This amount is consistent with the cap set forth in the Prenuptial Agreement, which provides that for marriages lasting ten (10) or more years, spousal maintenance shall not exceed \$15,000 per month for a period not to exceed five (5) years. The Parties have agreed to a four (4)-year term as part of this global settlement.

367-**Section 5.2 --- Method of Payment.** Spousal maintenance payments shall be due on the first day of each calendar month during the maintenance period. Payments shall be made by electronic funds transfer to a bank account designated by the Wife in writing. The Wife shall provide wire transfer or direct deposit instructions to the Husband in advance of the first payment. In the event that a payment due date falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or federal holiday, the payment shall be due on the immediately preceding business day.

379-Upon the occurrence of any termination event, the Husband\'s obligation to make any further maintenance payments shall cease immediately, and no further payments shall be due or owing. The Husband shall not be entitled to a refund or credit of any maintenance payments made prior to the termination event.

381:**Section 5.4 --- Tax Treatment.** The Parties acknowledge that under the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017, as codified in IRC § 71 (as amended) and IRC § 215 (as repealed for instruments executed after December 31, 2018), spousal maintenance payments made pursuant to a divorce or separation instrument executed after December 31, 2018, are **not deductible by the payor** and are **not includable in the gross income of the payee**. This Agreement having been executed on May 12, 2023, the spousal maintenance payments set forth herein shall be treated accordingly. The Parties acknowledge that this tax treatment has been taken into account in the negotiation and determination of the overall settlement.

383-**Section 5.5 --- Non-Modifiability.** The spousal maintenance provisions of this Agreement, including without limitation the amount, duration, and termination provisions, shall not be subject to modification by either Party or by the Court, whether for changes in financial circumstances or for any other reason, except as expressly provided in Section 5.3. The Parties expressly waive any right to seek modification of the spousal maintenance provisions set forth herein, and this waiver is made knowingly, voluntarily, and with the advice of counsel.

423:**Section 7.1 --- Basic Child Support.** The Husband shall pay to the Wife child support in the amount of **\$8,500 per month per child**, for a total of **\$17,000 per month** for both Children combined. Payments shall commence on the first day of the first full calendar month following the entry of the Judgment of Divorce. This child support obligation supersedes and replaces the temporary (pendente lite) child support order of \$14,000 per month entered by the Court on September 30, 2022. The Parties acknowledge that the child support amount set forth herein has been calculated by reference to the factors set forth in DRL § 240(1-b) and reflects the Parties\' agreement as to the appropriate level of support for the Children in light of the Husband\'s income, the Wife\'s income, and the Children\'s needs.

425-**Section 7.2 --- Duration.** The Husband\'s obligation to pay child support for each child shall continue until the earlier of: (a) the child\'s attainment of the age of eighteen (18); or (b) the child\'s graduation from high school, whichever occurs later, unless the child is sooner emancipated by marriage, entry into the military, or other legally recognized event constituting emancipation under New York law. In the event that a child becomes emancipated, the Husband\'s child support obligation for that child shall terminate effective as of the date of emancipation, and the monthly payment shall be reduced to \$8,500 per month for the remaining child.

153:> **(a) Royalty Floor.** Beginning with calendar year 2026, and for each full calendar year thereafter during the term of this Agreement, the minimum annual Running Royalty payable by Solstice to Apex shall be Five Hundred Thousand United States Dollars (\$500,000) (the \"**Royalty Floor**\"). If the aggregate Running Royalty payments actually due and paid with respect to Net Sales for a given calendar year are less than the Royalty Floor, Solstice shall pay the difference between the actual aggregate Running Royalty and the Royalty Floor within thirty (30) days following the end of such calendar year. For the avoidance of doubt, the Royalty Floor shall not apply to the partial calendar year 2025 (i.e., the period from the Effective Date through December 31, 2025), nor to any partial calendar year at the end of the term resulting from the expiration of the last Licensed Patent. The Royalty Floor shall be prorated for any partial calendar year at the end of the term.

155-> **(b) Royalty Cap.** The maximum aggregate Running Royalty payable by Solstice to Apex in any single calendar year shall not exceed One Million Eight Hundred Thousand United States Dollars (\$1,800,000) (the \"**Royalty Cap**\"). Once cumulative Running Royalty payments for a given calendar year reach the Royalty Cap, no further Running Royalty shall be due or payable for the remainder of that calendar year. The Royalty Cap shall be prorated for any partial calendar year at the beginning or end of the term.

159-> **(d) Royalty Payments.** Running Royalty payments shall be due and payable within forty-five (45) days after the end of each Calendar Quarter, concurrently with the delivery of the corresponding royalty report. All Running Royalty payments shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds to a bank account designated by Apex in writing from time to time. Apex shall provide Solstice with its initial wire instructions within five (5) business days of the Effective Date and shall provide not less than fifteen (15) days\' prior written notice of any change in wire instructions. All Running Royalty payments shall be made in United States Dollars. To the extent any Net Sales are invoiced in a currency other than United States Dollars, such amounts shall be converted to United States Dollars at the average daily exchange rate published by the European Central Bank for the applicable Calendar Quarter.

161:**Section 3.3 --- Tax Treatment.** The Parties agree and acknowledge that the Lump-Sum Payment constitutes consideration for the settlement and release of all claims in the Action and for the grant of the Patent License Agreement and the Covenant Not to Sue, and that the Running Royalty constitutes license royalties for the use of intellectual property rights. Each Party shall be solely responsible for the payment of all taxes, duties, assessments, and other governmental charges imposed on it in connection with the payments made or received under this Agreement. Solstice shall comply with all applicable withholding tax obligations under United States federal, state, and local tax law and under the laws of Ireland, including any applicable provisions of the Convention between the Government of the United States of America and the Government of Ireland for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income and Capital Gains (the \"**U.S.-Ireland Tax Treaty**\"). Apex shall reasonably cooperate with Solstice\'s requests for tax documentation, including the execution and delivery of IRS Form W-9 or such other forms as may be reasonably required to establish Apex\'s tax status and to enable Solstice to comply with its withholding obligations. In the event that any withholding is required, Solstice shall remit the withheld amounts to the appropriate governmental authority, provide Apex with documentation of such withholding, and the net amount received by Apex after such withholding shall be deemed to satisfy Solstice\'s payment obligation with respect to the amount so withheld.

163-**Section 3.4 --- No Coverage by Insurance.** The Parties acknowledge and agree that the Lump-Sum Payment, the Running Royalty, and all other payment obligations of Solstice under this Article III are not covered by, and Solstice does not expect to receive reimbursement from, any insurance policy maintained by Solstice or any of its Affiliates, including but not limited to intellectual property insurance Policy No. HSI-IP-2023-04891 issued by Halcyon Specialty Insurance Co. or any other insurance policy. Solstice\'s obligation to make all payments under this Article III is absolute and unconditional and shall not be contingent upon, reduced by, or subject to any right of set-off, counterclaim, or deduction related to insurance coverage, insurance reimbursement, or any dispute between Solstice and any insurer.

189-**Section 6.2 --- Cost of Audit.** The cost of any audit conducted pursuant to Section 6.1, including the fees and expenses of the independent auditing firm, shall be borne solely by Apex; provided, however, that if such audit reveals an underpayment of Running Royalties by Solstice exceeding five percent (5%) of the aggregate amount of Running Royalties that were due and payable for any audited period (as determined on an annualized basis), then Solstice shall bear and promptly reimburse Apex for the reasonable cost of such audit, including all fees and expenses of the auditing firm.

191:**Section 6.3 --- Underpayment / Overpayment.** In the event that an audit conducted pursuant to Section 6.1 reveals an underpayment of Running Royalties by Solstice, Solstice shall pay to Apex the full amount of such underpayment within thirty (30) days of written notice from Apex setting forth the audit findings and the amount of the underpayment, together with interest on such underpaid amount calculated at the rate set forth in Section 3.1(c) from the date such payment was originally due until the date of actual payment. In the event that an audit reveals an overpayment of Running Royalties by Solstice, such overpayment shall, at Solstice\'s sole election, be either (x) credited against future Running Royalty payments due from Solstice to Apex under Section 3.2, or (y) refunded by Apex to Solstice by wire transfer within thirty (30) days of written notice from Solstice electing a refund.

193-**Section 6.4 --- Confidentiality of Audit.** Prior to commencing any audit under this Article VI, the independent auditing firm engaged by Apex shall execute a confidentiality agreement, in form and substance reasonably acceptable to Solstice, limiting the disclosure of any information obtained during the audit to the following: (a) the fact and amount of any underpayment or overpayment of Running Royalties; and (b) a summary of the auditing firm\'s findings and conclusions necessary to support any claim of underpayment or overpayment. The auditing firm shall not disclose to Apex or to any other person or entity any detailed financial information, customer lists, pricing data, sales volumes by customer, or other competitively sensitive business information of Solstice obtained during the audit, except to the extent such information is strictly necessary to calculate and report the amount of any underpayment or overpayment. Solstice shall have the right to review and approve any audit report before it is delivered to Apex, solely for the purpose of verifying compliance with the confidentiality restrictions set forth in this Section 6.4.

295-**Section 13.7 --- Counterparts.** This Agreement may be executed in two or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which, taken together, shall constitute one and the same instrument. Execution and delivery of this Agreement by facsimile, electronic mail (including .pdf or .tiff format), or other electronic transmission (including through any electronic signature platform compliant with the U.S. ESIGN Act or the Irish Electronic Commerce Act 2000) shall be deemed to constitute delivery of an original executed counterpart and shall be valid and binding upon the Party so executing for all purposes.

297:**Section 13.8 --- No Admission of Liability.** This Agreement is entered into solely for the purpose of settling the Action and resolving the disputes between the Parties relating to the Asserted Patents and the Accused Products, and for no other purpose. Neither the execution of this Agreement, the performance of any obligation hereunder, the payment of any amount hereunder, nor any other aspect of this Agreement or the settlement of the Action shall be construed, deemed, or treated as an admission or concession by any Party of any liability, fault, infringement, invalidity, unenforceability, inequitable conduct, wrongdoing, or violation of law with respect to any matter, including without limitation the merits of any claim or defense in the Action. This Agreement shall not be offered or received in evidence in any proceeding as an admission or concession of liability, except in a proceeding to enforce its terms.

299-**Section 13.9 --- No Third-Party Beneficiaries.** This Agreement is entered into solely for the benefit of the Parties and their respective permitted successors and assigns, and nothing in this Agreement, express or implied, is intended to or shall confer upon any other person or entity any legal or equitable right, benefit, interest, or remedy of any nature whatsoever under or by reason of this Agreement, except as expressly provided herein with respect to Affiliates and indemnified persons under Article XI. Without limiting the foregoing, no officer, director, employee, agent, or representative of any Party shall be deemed a third-party beneficiary of this Agreement.

The Parties acknowledge that actual damages from a breach of the modified non-competition obligations would be difficult to ascertain and that the foregoing amounts represent a reasonable estimate of such damages.\"\] \[**WND/Blackhall Objection**: Both WND and Blackhall object to the inclusion of this liquidated damages provision on the grounds that: (i) the proposed amounts are disproportionate and punitive in nature; (ii) Delaware law requires a reasonable relationship between liquidated damages and actual or anticipated loss, and the proposed amounts have not been justified by such analysis; and (iii) the availability of injunctive relief and contempt remedies under the Consent Order provides CRH with adequate protection. WND and Blackhall contend that the provision would be unenforceable as a penalty clause under Delaware law.\] \[**C&H Note**: CRH is considering whether to retain, modify, or withdraw this proposal. If retained, CRH may need to provide a damages analysis supporting the reasonableness of the proposed amounts. This provision remains bracketed pending resolution.\]

401-**Section 12.3 --- Cumulative Remedies.** All remedies available to the Parties under this Agreement, at law, or in equity are cumulative and not exclusive, and the exercise of any one remedy shall not preclude or waive the right to pursue any other remedy. No single exercise of any remedy shall exhaust the non-breaching Party\'s right to seek the same or different remedies for any subsequent breach.

CRH is reviewing this language and may accept with modifications, including a requirement that a contemporaneous log be maintained and made available to CRH. *Status: Under CRH review.*

901:2\. **Section 4.1 --- Payment Period.** Blackhall has requested a forty-five (45)-day payment period for the Settlement Payment. CRH has counter-proposed thirty (30) days, which is reflected in the current draft. *Status: Under negotiation. CRH has indicated flexibility to accept 35 days as a compromise.*

903-3\. **Section 8.3(c) --- Knowledge Qualifier.** WND has requested the addition of \"to the best of his or her knowledge and belief, after reasonable inquiry\" to the Individual Defendants\' representation regarding completeness of data disclosure. CRH\'s position is that an unqualified representation is appropriate given the seriousness of the data exfiltration. *Status: Under CRH review. CRH may accept a modified qualifier such as \"to the best of his or her knowledge and belief, after diligent inquiry.\"*

51:**Section 2.1 --- Payment Amount.** In consideration of the mutual covenants, releases, and agreements set forth in this Agreement, Cascade shall pay to Vantor the Settlement Amount of Fourteen Million Seven Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars and No Cents (\$14,750,000.00) in full and final satisfaction of all Released Claims. 53:**Section 2.2 --- Payment Method and Timing.** The Settlement Amount shall be paid by Cascade to Vantor by wire transfer of immediately available funds in United States Dollars to a bank account designated by Vantor in writing. Vantor shall provide Cascade with complete and accurate wire transfer instructions, including the name of the receiving financial institution, ABA routing number, account number, account name, and any required reference information, within five (5) business days following the full execution and delivery of this Agreement by both Parties. Cascade shall cause the wire transfer of the full Settlement Amount to be initiated within thirty (30) calendar days following the Effective Date. Cascade\'s payment obligation shall be deemed satisfied upon confirmation by Cascade\'s bank that the wire transfer has been initiated in accordance with the wire instructions provided by Vantor. In the event that Vantor fails to provide wire transfer instructions within the time period specified herein, the thirty (30) calendar day payment deadline shall be extended on a day-for-day basis until the wire instructions are received by Cascade.

55:**Section 2.3 --- Tax Treatment.** The Parties make no representations or warranties regarding the tax characterization or tax treatment of the Settlement Amount under federal, state, local, or foreign tax law. Each Party shall be solely responsible for the payment of any and all taxes, including income taxes, penalties, and interest, owed by such Party in connection with the receipt or payment of the Settlement Amount. Vantor shall be solely responsible for determining whether the issuance of any IRS Form 1099 or other tax reporting form is required in connection with its receipt of the Settlement Amount, and, if so required, for the timely issuance thereof. Neither Party shall have any obligation to indemnify or hold harmless the other Party with respect to any tax liability arising from the receipt or payment of the Settlement Amount.

57:**Section 2.4 --- Source of Funds.** The Settlement Amount shall be funded from Cascade\'s operating funds and applicable insurance proceeds. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the source or sources from which Cascade funds the Settlement Amount shall not affect, diminish, or otherwise modify Cascade\'s obligation to make timely payment of the full Settlement Amount to Vantor in accordance with Section 2.2. In the event that any insurer fails or refuses to fund any portion of the Settlement Amount, Cascade shall remain solely and fully responsible for payment of the entire Settlement Amount.

61:**Section 3.1 --- No Admission by Cascade.** This Agreement, the payment of the Settlement Amount, and the settlement of the Action shall not constitute, and shall not be construed as, an admission of liability, wrongdoing, fault, negligence, or any violation of any statute, regulation, or rule of law by Cascade or any of the Cascade Released Parties. The Parties acknowledge that Cascade is entering into this Agreement solely to avoid the expense, burden, inconvenience, distraction, and uncertainty associated with continued litigation.

63:**Section 3.2 --- No Admission by Vantor.** This Agreement shall not constitute, and shall not be construed as, a concession, admission, or acknowledgment by Vantor that any of its claims asserted in the Action lacked merit, were frivolous, were brought in bad faith, or were otherwise deficient in any respect. The Parties acknowledge that Vantor is entering into this Agreement in the exercise of its reasonable business judgment and in consideration of the Settlement Amount and the other terms and conditions set forth herein.

65:**Section 3.3 --- Inadmissibility.** This Agreement, including all of its terms and conditions, the negotiations and discussions leading to the execution of this Agreement, the Settlement Amount, and any statements, offers, or representations made by either Party or its counsel during the course of settlement negotiations shall be inadmissible in any judicial, arbitral, administrative, or other legal proceeding for any purpose, including but not limited to as evidence of liability, wrongdoing, or the validity or invalidity of any claim or defense. 77:**2.1** **Settlement Amount.** In full and final settlement of all claims and counterclaims asserted or that could have been asserted in the Action, and all other Released Claims as defined herein, the Thalassa Parties shall pay, or cause to be paid, to Northwind the aggregate Settlement Amount of Seven Million Eight Hundred Fifty Thousand United States Dollars (\$7,850,000), payable in three (3) installments as follows:

79-> **(a)** *First Installment.* Four Million United States Dollars (\$4,000,000), to be deposited by wire transfer of immediately available funds into the Escrow Account within thirty (30) calendar days of the Effective Date (i.e., on or before December 20, 2024).

83-> **(c)** *Third Installment.* One Million Eight Hundred Fifty Thousand United States Dollars (\$1,850,000), to be deposited by wire transfer of immediately available funds into the Escrow Account within one hundred fifty (150) calendar days of the Effective Date (i.e., on or before April 19, 2025).
85:The obligation to pay the Settlement Amount shall be a joint and several obligation of the Thalassa Parties.

87:**2.2** **Escrow Mechanism.** All installments of the Settlement Amount shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds in United States Dollars to Escrow Account No. ESC-2024-NYK-08831 at Atlantic Fiduciary Trust Company, in accordance with the wire transfer instructions set forth in the Escrow Agreement. Each installment deposited into the Escrow Account shall be released to Northwind by the Escrow Agent promptly upon receipt of joint written instructions from counsel for the Parties, being Calderwood & Harkness LLP (counsel for the Thalassa Parties) and Hargrove, Delacroix & Stern LLP (counsel for Northwind), in accordance with the terms and conditions of the Escrow Agreement. Any interest earned on funds held in the Escrow Account shall be distributed to the Party ultimately entitled to receive the underlying principal in accordance with the Escrow Agreement.

89:**2.3** **Funding Sources.** The source of the Settlement Amount shall be determined by the Thalassa Parties in their sole and absolute discretion. The Parties acknowledge that portions of the Settlement Amount may be funded by contributions from Thalassa\'s protection and indemnity insurer, Oceanus Mutual Protection & Indemnity Club, or from other insurance carriers maintained by the Thalassa Parties. The Parties further acknowledge and agree that any insurance-related arrangements, including the terms, timing, and conditions of insurance contributions, are solely between the Thalassa Parties and their respective insurers and do not in any way affect, diminish, or condition the Thalassa Parties\' obligations to pay the Settlement Amount to Northwind in full and on the schedule set forth herein. In no event shall any dispute between the Thalassa Parties and their insurers excuse or delay the Thalassa Parties\' payment obligations under this Agreement.

91:**2.4** **Taxes.** Each Party shall be solely responsible for its own tax obligations, if any, arising from the receipt or payment of the Settlement Amount, including any applicable income, withholding, value-added, or other taxes imposed by any governmental authority. No Party makes any representation or warranty to any other Party regarding the tax treatment or tax consequences of the Settlement Amount or any payment made hereunder. Each Party agrees to indemnify and hold harmless the other Parties from any tax liability, penalty, or interest arising from such Party\'s failure to comply with its own tax obligations in connection with this Agreement.
93-**[ARTICLE 3 --- WAIVER OF COUNTERCLAIM]{.underline}**

95:**3.1** **Release of Counterclaim.** Contemporaneously with the execution of this Agreement and as part of the consideration for the mutual release set forth in Article 4 and the payment of the Settlement Amount, the Thalassa Parties hereby irrevocably waive, release, and forever discharge all claims asserted in the Counterclaim, including, without limitation, the claim for One Million Six Hundred Twenty Thousand United States Dollars (\$1,620,000) in unpaid hire for the period October 1 through December 31, 2022, and all claims arising therefrom, related thereto, or that could have been asserted in connection therewith. The Thalassa Parties acknowledge and agree that this waiver is unconditional and is not contingent upon the receipt of any portion of the Settlement Amount.

97:**3.2** **No Offset.** For the avoidance of doubt, the Settlement Amount of Seven Million Eight Hundred Fifty Thousand United States Dollars (\$7,850,000) is payable by the Thalassa Parties to Northwind in full, without any offset, deduction, setoff, recoupment, or counterclaim on account of the Counterclaim or any other claim, demand, or cause of action that the Thalassa Parties may have or claim to have against Northwind, whether arising under the Charter-Party, at law, in equity, in admiralty, or otherwise. The Thalassa Parties expressly waive any right of setoff or recoupment with respect to the Settlement Amount.

103-**4.2** **Release by the Thalassa Parties.** Effective upon the Effective Date, each of the Thalassa Parties, for itself and on behalf of its respective parents, subsidiaries, affiliates, predecessors, successors, assigns, officers, directors, members, managers, shareholders, employees, agents, attorneys, accountants, advisors, consultants, and representatives, and each of their respective heirs, executors, administrators, successors, and assigns (collectively, the \"Thalassa Releasors\"), hereby fully, finally, and irrevocably releases, acquits, and forever discharges Northwind and its parents, subsidiaries, affiliates, predecessors, successors, assigns, officers, directors, members, managers, shareholders, employees, agents, insurers, attorneys, accountants, advisors, consultants, and representatives, and each of their respective heirs, executors, administrators, successors, and assigns (collectively, the \"Northwind Releasees\"), from any and all Released Claims, including, without limitation, all claims asserted or that could have been asserted in the Counterclaim or otherwise in the Action.
129-**[ARTICLE 5 --- CONFIDENTIALITY]{.underline}**

131:**5.1** **Confidentiality Obligation.** The Parties agree that the terms and conditions of this Agreement, the Settlement Amount, the payment schedule, the mediation proceedings and submissions, and all negotiations, communications, and discussions leading to this Agreement (collectively, \"Confidential Information\") shall be kept strictly confidential and shall not be disclosed to any third party, except as expressly provided in Section 5.2 below. Each Party shall take reasonable steps to ensure that its officers, directors, employees, agents, and representatives who receive Confidential Information maintain the confidentiality thereof in accordance with this Article 5.
133-**5.2** **Permitted Disclosures.** Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 5.1, each Party may disclose Confidential Information:

149-**5.3** **Prior Notice of Required Disclosure.** If a Party is required to disclose Confidential Information pursuant to Section 5.2(f), such Party shall, to the extent legally permissible, provide the other Parties with prompt written notice of such requirement prior to making any such disclosure, together with a description of the information to be disclosed, in order to afford the other Parties a reasonable opportunity to seek a protective order, confidentiality agreement, or other appropriate remedy. If such protective order or other remedy is not obtained, or if the other Parties waive compliance with the terms of this Section 5.3, the disclosing Party shall furnish only that portion of the Confidential Information that, in the opinion of its legal counsel, is legally required to be disclosed and shall exercise commercially reasonable efforts to obtain assurances that confidential treatment will be accorded to the information so disclosed.

151:**5.4** **Public Statements.** Neither any Party nor its counsel shall issue any press release, public statement, public filing, or social media posting regarding this Agreement, the Settlement Amount, or the settlement of the Action without the prior written consent of the other Parties, which consent may be withheld in such Party\'s sole and absolute discretion. If any public statement is required by applicable law, regulation, or stock exchange rule, the Parties shall consult with each other and agree upon the content and timing of such statement prior to its issuance. Nothing in this Section 5.4 shall prevent any Party from stating, in response to any inquiry, that the Action has been resolved to the mutual satisfaction of the Parties.
153-**[ARTICLE 6 --- DISCONTINUANCE AND WITHDRAWAL OF MOTIONS]{.underline}**

157-**6.2** **Vacatur of Scheduled Appearances.** Within five (5) business days of the Effective Date, the Parties, through their respective counsel, shall jointly advise the Court and the chambers of the Honorable Lorraine K. Chen, J.S.C., that the Action has been settled and that the oral argument on the Thalassa Parties\' Motion for Partial Summary Judgment, currently scheduled for December 6, 2024, and any other scheduled court appearances, should be taken off the calendar and vacated.

159:**6.3** **Stipulation of discontinuance.** Within ten (10) business days of the Final Payment Date (i.e., the date of receipt and release of the third and final installment of the Settlement Amount in accordance with Section 2.1(c) and the Escrow Agreement), the Parties shall execute and cause to be filed with the Court the Stipulation of discontinuance With Prejudice in the form annexed hereto as **Exhibit C**, discontinuing the Action with prejudice, including all claims, counterclaims, cross-claims, and affirmative defenses, without costs to any Party except as otherwise expressly provided in this Agreement. Each Party shall bear its own costs, attorneys\' fees, and expenses in connection with the Action, except as otherwise provided herein.

161-**6.4** **Retention of Jurisdiction.** Contemporaneously with the filing of the stipulation described in Section 6.1, the Parties shall submit to the Court a stipulation and proposed order, substantially in the form annexed hereto as **Exhibit B**, providing that the Court shall retain jurisdiction over the Action and the Parties for a period of one hundred eighty (180) days following the Effective Date (i.e., through May 19, 2025) for the sole and limited purpose of enforcing the terms and conditions of this Agreement, including, without limitation, the entry of the Consent Judgment upon the occurrence of a Payment Default as provided in Article 7. Such stipulation and order shall provide that, following the expiration of said 180-day period, the Court\'s retained jurisdiction shall terminate, provided that no Payment Default has occurred and no enforcement proceeding is then pending.
163-**[ARTICLE 7 --- DEFAULT AND CONSENT JUDGMENT]{.underline}**

165:**7.1** **Timely Payment Required.** The Parties expressly acknowledge and agree that time is of the essence with respect to each installment of the Settlement Amount due under Section 2.1. The failure to make any installment payment on or before its due date shall constitute a material breach of this Agreement, subject to the Cure Period set forth in Section 7.2.

167:**7.2** **Payment Default.** A \"Payment Default\" shall occur if any installment of the Settlement Amount is not deposited into the Escrow Account in the full amount required on or before the applicable due date set forth in Section 2.1, and such failure is not cured within ten (10) business days after such due date (each such ten (10) business day period, a \"Cure Period\"). A Payment Default shall be deemed to have occurred automatically upon the expiration of the applicable Cure Period without the need for any demand, notice of default, or other communication from Northwind to the Thalassa Parties. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if the Thalassa Parties demonstrate that the failure to make timely payment was caused solely by an error in wire transfer processing by the transmitting or receiving bank, and the Thalassa Parties initiated the wire transfer on or before the applicable due date, such failure shall not constitute a Payment Default, provided that the full installment amount is deposited into the Escrow Account within the Cure Period.

169:**7.3** **Consent Judgment.** Upon the occurrence of a Payment Default, Northwind shall be entitled, without further notice to or demand upon the Thalassa Parties and without the necessity of any further proceeding, to present the Consent Judgment annexed hereto as **Exhibit D** to the Court for entry against the Thalassa Parties, jointly and severally, in the amount of the then-unpaid balance of the Settlement Amount, together with interest thereon at the rate of nine percent (9%) per annum (the statutory rate under New York law, as provided in CPLR Section 5004), calculated from the date of the Payment Default through the date of payment. The Thalassa Parties hereby irrevocably consent to the entry of the Consent Judgment in such amount and waive any and all defenses, objections, or challenges to the entry thereof, including any defense based on personal jurisdiction, improper venue, insufficiency of process, or insufficiency of service of process. The Thalassa Parties further acknowledge and agree that the Consent Judgment, once entered, shall be a final judgment enforceable in any court of competent jurisdiction.

171:**7.4** **Acceleration.** Upon the occurrence of a Payment Default with respect to any installment, all remaining unpaid installments of the Settlement Amount shall become immediately due and payable in full, without further notice or demand, and shall bear interest at the rate specified in Section 7.3 from the date of the Payment Default.

173:**7.5** **Costs of Enforcement.** In the event of a Payment Default, the Thalassa Parties shall be responsible for and shall promptly reimburse Northwind for all reasonable and documented costs and expenses, including reasonable attorneys\' fees and disbursements, expert fees, court costs, and other expenses, incurred by Northwind in connection with the enforcement of this Agreement, the collection of the unpaid Settlement Amount, and the entry, domestication, and enforcement of the Consent Judgment in any jurisdiction.
175-**[ARTICLE 8 --- REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES]{.underline}**

137:**[ARTICLE 3 --- SETTLEMENT PAYMENTS]{.underline}**

139:**Section 3.1** *Payment Schedule.* In full and complete settlement of all claims, counterclaims, and disputes between the Parties arising out of or related to the Charter-Party, the Vessel, and the Action, the TSL Parties shall pay to Northwind an aggregate amount of Seven Million Eight Hundred Fifty Thousand United States Dollars (\$7,850,000) (the \"Settlement Amount\"), payable in three (3) installments as follows:

141-> \(a\) *First Payment.* The sum of Four Million United States Dollars (\$4,000,000) (the \"First Payment\"), which shall be due and payable within thirty (30) calendar days of the Effective Date. The First Payment shall be deposited by wire transfer of immediately available funds into the Escrow Account.

149-**Section 3.2** *Escrow Arrangements.* All payments made pursuant to Section 3.1 shall be effected by wire transfer of immediately available United States Dollars to the Escrow Account (Account No. ESC-2024-NYK-08831) maintained by Atlantic Fiduciary Trust Company at 60 Wall Street, Suite 2800, New York, NY 10005. The wire transfer instructions for the Escrow Account are set forth in Exhibit D attached hereto. The release of funds from the Escrow Account to Northwind shall be governed by the terms and conditions of the Escrow Agreement, which shall be entered into substantially contemporaneously with the execution of this Agreement. Release of funds from the Escrow Account to Northwind shall require joint written instruction of the Parties, or as otherwise provided in the Escrow Agreement (including, without limitation, any provision for unilateral disbursement upon certification of compliance with the conditions set forth therein). The primary contact for all matters relating to the Escrow Account and the Escrow Agreement shall be Martin Schreiber, Vice President, Escrow Services, Atlantic Fiduciary Trust Company, 60 Wall Street, Suite 2800, New York, NY 10005 (telephone: (212) 555-3400; email: mschreiber@atlanticfiduciary.com). All fees, costs, and expenses of the Escrow Agent incurred in connection with the Escrow Agreement and the maintenance and administration of the Escrow Account shall be borne equally by the TSL Parties, on the one hand, and Northwind, on the other hand.
151:**Section 3.3** *Funding Sources.* The Settlement Amount shall be funded from the following sources:
153-> \(a\) *TSL Corporate Funds.* TSL corporate funds in the aggregate amount of Five Million Three Hundred Fifty Thousand United States Dollars (\$5,350,000).

155-> \(b\) *P&I Contribution.* A contribution from Oceanus Mutual Protection & Indemnity Club in the aggregate amount of Two Million Five Hundred Thousand United States Dollars (\$2,500,000) (the \"P&I Contribution\"), payable under Policy No. OCE-P&I-2020-TSL-0047, subject to the approval of the Oceanus P&I Club Board of Directors (such approval being expected on or about November 22, 2024).

157:The allocation of the funding sources set forth in clauses (a) and (b) above among the three payment installments described in Section 3.1 shall be at the sole discretion of the TSL Parties, provided that the aggregate amounts and payment deadlines set forth in Section 3.1 are satisfied in full. Northwind acknowledges that the P&I Contribution is subject to the approval of the Board of Directors of Oceanus Mutual Protection & Indemnity Club and agrees that any delay in obtaining such Board approval shall not, in and of itself, constitute a default or Event of Default hereunder, provided that (i) the TSL Parties use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain such Board approval as promptly as practicable, and (ii) the aggregate payment schedule set forth in Section 3.1, including all deadlines therein, is not delayed or otherwise adversely affected. For the avoidance of doubt, the TSL Parties remain fully and unconditionally responsible for payment of the entire Settlement Amount regardless of whether, or to what extent, the P&I Contribution is approved or funded.

159:**Section 3.4** *TSL Counterclaim Waiver.* As an integral part of the settlement contemplated by this Agreement, and in consideration of the mutual covenants set forth herein, the TSL Parties hereby irrevocably waive, release, and abandon the TSL Counterclaim for One Million Six Hundred Twenty Thousand United States Dollars (\$1,620,000) in unpaid hire for the period October 1 through December 31, 2022, as asserted in the Verified Answer and Counterclaim filed in the Action on November 17, 2023. The Parties acknowledge and agree that the payment of the Settlement Amount by the TSL Parties and the waiver of the TSL Counterclaim together constitute the full, final, and complete resolution of all financial obligations between and among the Parties arising out of or relating to the Charter-Party, the Vessel, and the Action. No further sums shall be due or payable by any Party to any other Party on account of any matter arising out of or related to the Charter-Party, the Vessel, or the Action, except as expressly provided in this Agreement.

161:**Section 3.5** *Tax Treatment.* Each Party shall be solely responsible for the payment of any and all taxes, duties, levies, assessments, and other governmental charges (including, without limitation, income taxes, value-added taxes, withholding taxes, and any penalties or interest thereon) arising from or attributable to the receipt or payment of any portion of the Settlement Amount by such Party. Neither Party makes any representation or warranty to any other Party regarding the tax treatment, tax characterization, or tax consequences of the Settlement Amount or any installment thereof. No Party shall be required to withhold or deduct any portion of any payment of the Settlement Amount on account of any tax, duty, or other governmental charge, unless such withholding or deduction is required by applicable law, rule, or regulation. In the event that any Party determines in good faith that it is required by applicable law to withhold or deduct any amount from any payment made hereunder, such Party shall: (i) provide prompt written notice to the other Party or Parties of such determination, together with reasonable supporting documentation; (ii) remit the withheld amount to the appropriate governmental authority in accordance with applicable law; and (iii) provide the other Party or Parties with evidence of such remittance within a reasonable period of time.
163-**[ARTICLE 4 --- WITHDRAWAL OF PENDING MOTIONS AND DISCONTINUANCE]{.underline}**

239-> \(a\) *Payment Default.* Upon the occurrence of a Payment Default under Section 7.1(a), Northwind shall be entitled, in addition to all other remedies available at law, in equity, or in admiralty, to the following remedies:
241:> \(i\) *Acceleration.* To accelerate the entire unpaid balance of the Settlement Amount, which unpaid balance shall become immediately due and payable in full without further notice or demand;

243:> \(ii\) *Interest.* To recover interest on the unpaid balance of the Settlement Amount at the rate of nine percent (9%) per annum (the statutory rate of interest under Section 5004 of the New York Civil Practice Law and Rules), calculated from the date of the Payment Default until such unpaid balance is paid in full; and
245-> \(iii\) *Consent Judgment.* To file and enter the Consent Judgment as provided in Section 7.3.
251-**Section 7.3** *Consent Judgment.*

253:> \(a\) Contemporaneously with the execution of this Agreement, the TSL Parties shall execute a proposed Consent Judgment in favor of Northwind, substantially in the form attached hereto as **Exhibit C**, in the amount of the unpaid balance of the Settlement Amount, together with accrued interest at the rate of nine percent (9%) per annum (the New York statutory rate) computed from the date of any Payment Default through the date of entry of such Consent Judgment.

255-> \(b\) In the event of a Payment Default under Section 7.1(a), Northwind shall be entitled to file the executed Consent Judgment with the Court without further notice to or consent of the TSL Parties, and the TSL Parties hereby irrevocably consent to the entry of such Consent Judgment by the Court. The TSL Parties expressly waive any right to contest, oppose, or otherwise challenge the entry of the Consent Judgment, including, without limitation, any right to a hearing or to assert any defense or objection thereto.

257-> \(c\) The executed Consent Judgment shall be held in trust by Northwind\'s counsel, Hargrove, Delacroix & Stern LLP, at its offices located at 600 Lexington Avenue, 28th Floor, New York, NY 10022, and shall not be filed with the Court unless and until a Payment Default under Section 7.1(a) occurs.

259:> \(d\) Upon payment in full of the Settlement Amount (including any accrued interest, if applicable), Northwind shall promptly return the executed Consent Judgment to the TSL Parties\' counsel, Calderwood & Harkness LLP, for destruction, and shall provide written confirmation that no copy of the executed Consent Judgment has been retained by Northwind or its counsel.

261-**Section 7.4** *Attorneys\' Fees and Costs.* In any action, suit, or proceeding commenced by any Party to enforce the terms, provisions, or conditions of this Agreement, the prevailing Party shall be entitled to recover from the non-prevailing Party or Parties its reasonable attorneys\' fees, costs, and disbursements incurred in connection with such enforcement action, in addition to any other relief to which such prevailing Party may be entitled.

1: **[SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND MUTUAL RELEASE]{.underline}**
2: 
3: **(Execution Version)**
4: 
5: **April 22, 2024**
6: 
7: *Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC, et al.* Case No. 1021-00006 Circuit Court of the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County, Florida
8: 
9: CONFIDENTIAL --- SUBJECT TO CONFIDENTIALITY PROVISIONS OF ARTICLE XII

11: Right-click to update Table of Contents

13: **SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND MUTUAL RELEASE**
14: 
15: This **SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND MUTUAL RELEASE** (this \"Agreement\") is entered into and made effective as of April 22, 2024 (the \"Effective Date\"), by and among the following parties:
16: 
17: **VERIMARK HOSPITALITY GROUP INC.**, a Delaware corporation, with its principal place of business at 2400 East Las Olas Boulevard, Suite 3100, Fort Lauderdale, Florida 33301, and whose common stock is listed on the Nasdaq Stock Market under the ticker symbol \"VHMK\" (hereinafter referred to as \"Verimark\" or \"VHG\");
18: 
19: and
20: 
21: **COASTAL PALMS FRANCHISE HOLDINGS LLC**, a Florida limited liability company, with its principal office at 9500 Gulf Shore Drive, Suite 450, Naples, Florida 34108 (hereinafter referred to as \"Coastal Palms\" or \"CPFH\");
22: 
23: **RANDALL \"RANDY\" BRECKER**, an individual residing in the State of Florida, who serves as the Managing Member and holds a sixty percent (60%) equity interest in Coastal Palms, and who also serves as the President of Suncoast Room Management Inc. (hereinafter referred to as \"R. Brecker\");
24: 
25: **THERESA BRECKER**, an individual residing in the State of Florida, who is a Member of and holds a fifteen percent (15%) equity interest in Coastal Palms (hereinafter referred to as \"T. Brecker\");
26: 
27: **NOLAN PRESCOTT**, an individual residing in the State of Florida, who is a Member of and holds a twenty-five percent (25%) equity interest in Coastal Palms (hereinafter referred to as \"Prescott\");
28: 
29: **GULF BREEZE HOSPITALITY LLC**, a Florida limited liability company (hereinafter referred to as \"Gulf Breeze\");
30: 
31: **SAVANNAH LODGING PARTNERS LLC**, a Georgia limited liability company (hereinafter referred to as \"Savannah Lodging\");
32: 
33: **SUNCOAST ROOM MANAGEMENT INC.**, a Florida corporation (hereinafter referred to as \"Suncoast\");
34: 
35: Coastal Palms, R. Brecker, T. Brecker, Prescott, Gulf Breeze, Savannah Lodging, and Suncoast are collectively referred to herein as the \"Coastal Palms Parties.\" Verimark and the Coastal Palms Parties are collectively referred to herein as the \"Parties\" and each individually as a \"Party.\"
36: 
37: **[RECITALS]{.underline}**
38: 
39: **WHEREAS:**
40: 
41: **A. Franchise Relationship.** Verimark operates and franchises approximately 340 branded hotel properties across the southeastern United States under the \"Verimark Suites,\" \"Verimark Select,\" and \"Verimark Grand\" flags. For fiscal year 2021, Verimark reported consolidated revenue of approximately \$1.42 billion, of which the franchise segment contributed approximately \$218 million. Coastal Palms is the operator of twenty-two (22) franchised hotel properties --- eighteen (18) operating under the Verimark Suites flag and four (4) operating under the Verimark Select flag --- located across the States of Florida and Georgia, comprising approximately 3,740 total guest rooms. The first Franchise License Agreement (\"FLA\") between Verimark and Coastal Palms was executed on June 15, 2007, for a Verimark Suites property located in Naples, Florida. Over the following years, Coastal Palms and its affiliates executed a total of twenty-two (22) individual FLAs with Verimark, the most recent of which was dated September 3, 2019. Each FLA provides for a twenty (20)-year initial term and is governed by the laws of the State of Florida, with mandatory venue for any disputes in Broward County, Florida. Under each FLA, Coastal Palms is required to pay the following fees: (i) a royalty equal to five percent (5%) of Gross Room Revenue (\"GRR\") (FLA § 4.1); (ii) a marketing-fund contribution equal to two and one-half percent (2.5%) of GRR (FLA § 4.2); and (iii) a technology fee of twelve dollars and fifty cents (\$12.50) per available room per month, adjusted annually for changes in the Consumer Price Index, with such adjustment capped at three percent (3%) per year (FLA § 4.3). Late-payment interest under the FLAs accrues at a rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month, compounded monthly (FLA § 4.6). Additionally, FLA § 15.3 provides for liquidated damages upon termination for cause in an amount equal to three times (3×) the trailing-twelve-month royalties per property... (line truncated to 2000 chars)
42: 
43: **B. The Litigation.** On November 8, 2021, a former Coastal Palms regional controller, Janet Kerrigan, reported to Verimark\'s compliance hotline allegations of systematic revenue underreporting by the Coastal Palms Parties. In response, Verimark retained Thornbury & Associates CPAs LLP to conduct a franchise-compliance audit of the Coastal Palms properties. Thornbury\'s preliminary findings, delivered to Verimark on January 18, 2022, indicated that the audited properties had underreported GRR by approximately twenty-six percent (26%) for the period spanning fiscal years 2019 through 2021. Verimark issued a Notice of Material Breach to Coastal Palms on February 4, 2022, demanding that Coastal Palms cure the identified breaches within thirty (30) days in accordance with FLA § 14.1. Coastal Palms, through its counsel Whitfield, Barrow & Crane LLP, responded by letter dated February 28, 2022, denying any material breach and contesting the methodology and conclusions of the Thornbury audit. No cure was tendered by Coastal Palms within the thirty (30)-day period, which expired on March 6, 2022. On March 7, 2022, Verimark filed a ten-count Complaint in the Circuit Court of the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County, Florida, bearing Case Number 1021-00006 (the \"Litigation\"), asserting claims for: (i) breach of contract --- royalties; (ii) breach of contract --- marketing fund; (iii) breach of contract --- technology fees; (iv) breach of the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing; (v) fraudulent concealment; (vi) negligent misrepresentation; (vii) unjust enrichment; (viii) declaratory judgment; (ix) accounting; and (x) civil conspiracy. In the Complaint, Verimark claimed damages in the approximate aggregate amount of \$150,000,000, consisting of: (a) \$16,095,000 in direct underpayments of royalties, marketing-fund contributions, and technology fees; (b) \$28,400,000 in contractual late-payment interest calculated in accordance with FLA § 4.6; a... (line truncated to 2000 chars)
44: 
45: **C. Summary Judgment Ruling.** On February 9, 2024, the Court (the Honorable Richard M. Calloway, Circuit Judge) entered an Order granting Verimark\'s Motion for Partial Summary Judgment on Count I (Breach of Contract --- Royalties) and Count II (Breach of Contract --- Marketing Fund), finding as a matter of law that Coastal Palms\' exclusion of revenues collected by Suncoast Room Management Inc. from its calculation and reporting of GRR constituted a material breach of FLA §§ 4.1 and 4.2. The Court denied Coastal Palms\' Cross-Motion for Summary Judgment on all counts and deferred the determination of damages to trial.
46: 
47: **D. Mediation and Settlement.** On February 23, 2024, the Parties agreed to submit their dispute to mediation before the Honorable Patricia Everwood (Retired), of Everwood Dispute Resolution PLLC. A two-day mediation session was conducted on March 14 and 15, 2024, at 396 Alhambra Circle, Suite 800, Coral Gables, Florida 33134. A tentative settlement was reached on the second day of mediation, March 15, 2024, and the Parties executed a written term sheet memorializing the principal terms of the settlement on March 22, 2024. The Parties now desire to fully and finally resolve all claims and counterclaims in the Litigation, and all related disputes among the Parties, on the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement.
48: 
49: **E. Desire to Settle.** The Parties acknowledge the uncertainty, risk, and expense inherent in continued litigation and trial, and each Party has made an independent assessment of the merits and risks of its respective claims and defenses. The Parties desire to avoid the further burden and expense of trial and to resolve their disputes amicably and in full. Entry into this Agreement is not, and shall not be construed as, an admission of liability, wrongdoing, or the validity of any claim or defense by any Party. Each Party has been represented by competent legal counsel of its choosing in the negotiation and execution of this Agreement, and each Party has had a full and fair opportunity to review, analyze, and negotiate the terms set forth herein.
50: 
51: **NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual promises, covenants, releases, and agreements set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:
52: 
53: **[ARTICLE I --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**
54: 
55: As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Article I shall have the meanings ascribed to them elsewhere in this Agreement.
56: 
57: **1.1** \"**Agreement**\" means this Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release, together with all Exhibits and Schedules attached hereto, which are incorporated herein by reference and made a part hereof.
58: 
59: **1.2** \"**Closing**\" means the consummation of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement on the Closing Date, including the execution and delivery of this Agreement by all Parties, the payment of the Initial Payment, and the execution and delivery of all ancillary documents required to be delivered at or prior to the Closing.
60: 
61: **1.3** \"**Closing Date**\" means April 22, 2024.
62: 
63: **1.4** \"**Collateral Properties**\" means the eight (8) unencumbered hotel properties identified in Schedule 3.1 hereto, which serve as collateral for the security interest granted to Verimark pursuant to Article III.
64: 
65: **1.5** \"**Complaint**\" means the ten-count Complaint filed by Verimark on March 7, 2022, in Case No. 1021-00006, in the Circuit Court of the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County, Florida, together with all amendments thereto.
66: 
67: **1.6** \"**Counterclaim**\" means the \$12,000,000 counterclaim filed by Coastal Palms on April 18, 2022, in the Litigation, asserting claims for alleged brand-standard violations and over-billing.
68: 
69: **1.7** \"**Court**\" means the Circuit Court of the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County, Florida.
70: 
71: **1.8** \"**De-Identification Deadline**\" means August 20, 2024, which is one hundred twenty (120) days from the Closing Date.
72: 
73: **1.9** \"**Enhanced Audit Protocol**\" means the enhanced audit and reporting requirements applicable to the Retained Properties, as set forth in Article VIII of this Agreement and as more fully described in Exhibit D attached hereto.
74: 
75: **1.10** \"**Event of Default**\" has the meaning set forth in Section 2.7 of this Agreement.
76: 
77: **1.11** \"**Existing FLAs**\" means the twenty-two (22) Franchise License Agreements between Verimark and Coastal Palms and/or its affiliates (including Gulf Breeze and Savannah Lodging), the first of which was executed on June 15, 2007, and the most recent of which was executed on September 3, 2019, governing the operation of the Properties under the Verimark Brands.
78: 
79: **1.12** \"**GRR**\" or \"**Gross Room Revenue**\" has the meaning ascribed to such term in Section 4.1 of each FLA, which generally includes all revenue derived from or attributable to the rental of guest rooms at the applicable Property, regardless of the method of collection, booking channel, or collecting entity.
80: 
81: **1.13** \"**Initial Payment**\" means the cash payment of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000) payable by Coastal Palms to Verimark at Closing in accordance with Section 2.2 of this Agreement.
82: 
83: **1.14** \"**Ironclad**\" means Ironclad National Bank, a national banking association, which holds first-lien mortgage loans on eighteen (18) of the twenty-two (22) Properties, with an aggregate outstanding principal balance of approximately Ninety-Four Million Dollars (\$94,000,000) as of the date hereof.
84: 
85: **1.15** \"**Litigation**\" means the action styled *Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC, et al.*, Case No. 1021-00006, pending in the Circuit Court of the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County, Florida, including all claims, counterclaims, cross-claims, and third-party claims asserted therein.
86: 
87: **1.16** \"**New FLAs**\" means the new ten (10)-year Franchise License Agreements to be executed by Verimark and the applicable Coastal Palms Party for each of the Retained Properties, substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit C.
88: 
89: **1.17** \"**Payment Schedule**\" means the schedule of payments set forth in Article II and as more fully described in Exhibit A attached hereto.
90: 
91: **1.18** \"**Personal Guaranties**\" means the individual guaranty agreements to be executed by R. Brecker and Prescott, each substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit E, pursuant to which R. Brecker and Prescott jointly and severally guarantee all obligations of the Coastal Palms Parties under this Agreement.
92: 
93: **1.19** \"**Properties**\" means the twenty-two (22) hotel properties operated by the Coastal Palms Parties under the Existing FLAs.
94: 
95: **1.20** \"**Retained Properties**\" means the eight (8) Properties identified in Section 7.1 of this Agreement and in Exhibit C that will continue to be franchised under the New FLAs, consisting of four (4) properties in Naples, Florida; two (2) properties on Marco Island, Florida; and two (2) properties in Tampa, Florida.
96: 
97: **1.21** \"**Security Agreement**\" means the security agreement to be executed by Coastal Palms in favor of Verimark, substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit F, granting Verimark a first-priority security interest in the Collateral Properties to secure the Structured Payments and other obligations under this Agreement.
98: 
99: **1.22** \"**Settlement Amount**\" means the aggregate sum of Eighty-Seven Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$87,500,000), payable by the Coastal Palms Parties to Verimark in accordance with Article II of this Agreement.
100: 
101: **1.23** \"**Structured Payments**\" means the eight (8) semi-annual payments of Seven Million Eight Hundred Twelve Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$7,812,500) each, totaling Sixty-Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$62,500,000), payable in accordance with Section 2.3 of this Agreement, the first such payment being due on October 22, 2024, and the last such payment being due on April 22, 2028, as more fully described in the Payment Schedule attached hereto as Exhibit A.
102: 
103: **1.24** \"**Surrendered Properties**\" means the fourteen (14) Properties identified in Section 7.1 and Exhibit B of this Agreement that are subject to franchise surrender, de-identification, and termination of the applicable Existing FLAs.
104: 
105: **1.25** \"**Verimark Brands**\" means \"Verimark Suites,\" \"Verimark Select,\" and \"Verimark Grand,\" together with all associated trademarks, service marks, logos, trade dress, proprietary systems (including reservation systems, property management systems, and revenue management systems), and all other intellectual property owned, licensed, or controlled by Verimark in connection with the branding and operation of its franchised hotel properties.
106: 
107: **[ARTICLE II --- SETTLEMENT PAYMENT]{.underline}**
108: 
109: **Section 2.1 --- Total Settlement Amount.** In full and final settlement of all claims, counterclaims, causes of action, and disputes among the Parties, whether asserted or unasserted, known or unknown, arising from or relating to the Existing FLAs, the Litigation, or the subject matter thereof, the Coastal Palms Parties shall pay to Verimark a total Settlement Amount of Eighty-Seven Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$87,500,000), payable as follows:
110: 
111: > \(a\) The Initial Payment of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000), payable at the Closing in accordance with Section 2.2 below; and
112: >
113: > \(b\) The Structured Payments totaling Sixty-Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$62,500,000), payable in eight (8) semi-annual installments of Seven Million Eight Hundred Twelve Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$7,812,500) each, in accordance with Section 2.3 below.
114: 
115: The Payment Schedule setting forth the dates, amounts, and interest calculations for all payments under this Article II is attached hereto as Exhibit A and incorporated herein by reference.
116: 
117: **Section 2.2 --- Initial Payment.** On the Closing Date, Coastal Palms shall pay to Verimark the Initial Payment of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000) by wire transfer of immediately available funds from the escrow account established at Ironclad National Bank for the purposes of this settlement to Verimark\'s designated account. Verimark shall provide Coastal Palms with complete wire-transfer instructions for the designated receiving account no later than three (3) business days prior to the Closing Date. Upon receipt of the Initial Payment, Verimark\'s counsel, Calderwood & Harkness LLP, at 110 SE 6th Street, Suite 2800, Fort Lauderdale, Florida 33301, shall promptly issue a written confirmation of receipt to counsel for the Coastal Palms Parties. The obligation to make the Initial Payment is unconditional and shall not be subject to any right of setoff, counterclaim, defense, or deduction.
118: 
119: **Section 2.3 --- Structured Payments.** Following the payment of the Initial Payment, Coastal Palms shall pay to Verimark the remaining Sixty-Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$62,500,000) in eight (8) equal semi-annual installments of Seven Million Eight Hundred Twelve Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$7,812,500) each, on the following schedule:
120: 
121: > \(a\) The first installment shall be due and payable on October 22, 2024.
122: >
123: > \(b\) The second installment shall be due and payable on April 22, 2025.
124: >
125: > \(c\) The third installment shall be due and payable on October 22, 2025.
126: >
127: > \(d\) The fourth installment shall be due and payable on April 22, 2026.
128: >
129: > \(e\) The fifth installment shall be due and payable on October 22, 2026.
130: >
131: > \(f\) The sixth installment shall be due and payable on April 22, 2027.
132: >
133: > \(g\) The seventh installment shall be due and payable on October 22, 2027.
134: >
135: > \(h\) The eighth and final installment shall be due and payable on April 22, 2028.
136: 
137: All Structured Payments shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account designated by Verimark in accordance with the wire-transfer instructions provided pursuant to Section 2.2, or to such other account as Verimark may designate in writing from time to time upon not less than ten (10) business days\' prior notice to Coastal Palms.
138: 
139: **Section 2.4 --- Interest on Structured Payments.** Interest shall accrue on the outstanding principal balance of the Structured Payments at a rate of six and one-half percent (6.5%) per annum, simple interest, calculated on the basis of a 365-day year and the actual number of days elapsed. Interest shall begin to accrue on the Closing Date and shall be calculated on the then-outstanding principal balance of the Structured Payments. Interest payments shall be due and payable concurrently with each semi-annual installment payment. The amount of interest due with each installment shall be calculated by multiplying the outstanding principal balance as of the first day of the applicable interest period by the annual interest rate of 6.5%, and then multiplying the result by a fraction, the numerator of which is the actual number of days elapsed during such interest period and the denominator of which is 365. A detailed schedule setting forth the estimated interest amounts due with each installment is set forth in Exhibit A.
140: 
141: **Section 2.5 --- Late Payments.** Any Structured Payment (including any concurrent interest payment) not received by Verimark within ten (10) business days of its scheduled due date shall bear additional default interest at the rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month on the overdue amount, calculated from the original due date until the date on which such overdue amount is received by Verimark in full. This default interest shall be in addition to, and not in substitution for, the interest otherwise payable under Section 2.4. If Coastal Palms fails to cure a late payment within thirty (30) days after written notice from Verimark specifying the overdue payment and the amount due, such failure shall constitute an Event of Default under Section 2.7 of this Agreement. Nothing in this Section 2.5 shall be construed to extend the due date for any Structured Payment or to waive Verimark\'s right to declare an Event of Default following the expiration of the applicable cure period.
142: 
143: **Section 2.6 --- Prepayment.** Coastal Palms may, at its option, prepay all or any portion of the Structured Payments at any time without premium, penalty, or additional charge of any kind. Any partial prepayment shall be applied first to any accrued and unpaid interest on the outstanding principal balance of the Structured Payments, and second to the scheduled installments in inverse order of maturity (i.e., applied first to the most distant scheduled installment, then to the next most distant, and so on), thereby reducing the total interest obligation over the remaining term. Coastal Palms shall provide Verimark with not less than five (5) business days\' prior written notice of any prepayment, specifying the amount and intended date of such prepayment. Verimark shall recalculate the interest amounts due on any remaining installments following any partial prepayment and shall provide an updated Payment Schedule to Coastal Palms within ten (10) business days of receipt of any such prepayment.
144: 
145: **Section 2.7 --- Events of Default and Acceleration.** An \"Event of Default\" shall be deemed to have occurred upon the happening of any of the following:
146: 
147: > \(a\) **Payment Default.** Failure by any Coastal Palms Party to make any payment of the Structured Payments, accrued interest, or any other monetary obligation under this Agreement within thirty (30) days of the date on which Verimark delivers written notice to Coastal Palms specifying such payment default;
148: >
149: > \(b\) **Covenant Default.** Breach by any Coastal Palms Party of any material covenant, agreement, or obligation under this Agreement (other than a payment obligation, which is governed by clause (a) above) that remains uncured for thirty (30) days after Verimark delivers written notice to Coastal Palms specifying such breach in reasonable detail;
150: >
151: > \(c\) **Bankruptcy or Insolvency.** The commencement of any voluntary or involuntary proceeding under the United States Bankruptcy Code, Title 11, United States Code, or under any state insolvency, receivership, dissolution, or similar statute, by or against any Coastal Palms Party, or the appointment of a receiver, trustee, custodian, or similar official for the business, assets, or property of any Coastal Palms Party, or the making of a general assignment for the benefit of creditors by any Coastal Palms Party;
152: >
153: > \(d\) **Breach of Representations and Warranties.** Any representation or warranty made by any Coastal Palms Party in this Agreement or in any ancillary document delivered in connection herewith that is materially inaccurate, false, or misleading as of the date on which it was made, and such inaccuracy, falsity, or misleading character is not cured within thirty (30) days after written notice from Verimark specifying the same;
154: >
155: > \(e\) **De-Identification Failure.** Failure by any Coastal Palms Party to comply with the de-identification requirements set forth in Article VII of this Agreement by the De-Identification Deadline.
156: 
157: Upon the occurrence of an Event of Default, Verimark may, at its sole election and upon written notice to Coastal Palms, declare the entire outstanding principal balance of the Structured Payments, together with all accrued and unpaid interest thereon and all other amounts owing under this Agreement, immediately due and payable in full, without further notice, demand, presentment, or protest, all of which are hereby waived by the Coastal Palms Parties. Acceleration of the Structured Payments pursuant to this Section 2.7 shall not constitute a waiver of, or limit, any other rights or remedies available to Verimark at law or in equity, including, without limitation, the right to enforce the Security Agreement, to seek collection under the Personal Guaranties, to pursue foreclosure on the Collateral Properties, and to seek injunctive or other equitable relief from the Court.
158: 
159: **Section 2.8 --- Tax Treatment.** Each Party shall be solely responsible for the payment of all federal, state, and local taxes, and for the filing of all tax returns and reports, arising from or attributable to the payments received or made by such Party under this Agreement. The Parties agree that, for federal and state income-tax purposes, the Settlement Amount shall be treated by all Parties as compensatory damages and that no portion of the Settlement Amount shall be characterized as punitive damages, penalties, or interest for tax purposes, except to the extent required by applicable law. The Coastal Palms Parties shall be solely responsible for any and all withholding obligations, including but not limited to any obligation to withhold and remit taxes on behalf of Verimark, if any such obligation exists under applicable law. No Party shall take any position on any tax return or in any proceeding before any taxing authority that is inconsistent with the treatment described in this Section 2.8, unless required to do so by a final determination (as defined in Section 1313(a) of the Internal Revenue Code) of a court of competent jurisdiction or an applicable taxing authority.

163: **Section 3.1 --- Security Interest.** To secure the prompt and full payment and performance of all obligations of the Coastal Palms Parties under this Agreement, including, without limitation, the payment of all Structured Payments, accrued interest thereon, default interest, and any indemnification obligations arising under Article X, Coastal Palms hereby grants to Verimark a first-priority security interest in the eight (8) unencumbered hotel properties identified in Schedule 3.1 attached hereto (the \"Collateral Properties\"), together with all improvements, fixtures, furnishings, equipment, accounts, general intangibles, and proceeds related thereto (collectively, the \"Collateral\"). The aggregate appraised value of the Collateral Properties, as determined by independent appraisals conducted by licensed commercial real-estate appraisers within the ninety (90)-day period preceding the Closing Date, is not less than Seventy-One Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$71,200,000). The security interest granted hereunder shall be evidenced by the Security Agreement, which shall be substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit F and shall be executed and delivered concurrently with the execution of this Agreement.

The UCC-1 Financing Statement shall identify the following:

Brecker and Prescott shall each execute and deliver to Verimark a Personal Guaranty, substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit E, pursuant to which R. Brecker and Prescott shall jointly and severally, absolutely, unconditionally, and irrevocably guarantee the full and prompt payment and performance of all obligations of the Coastal Palms Parties under this Agreement, including, without limitation, all Structured Payments, accrued interest, default interest, indemnification obligations, and any and all other amounts that may become due and owing under this Agreement. Ironclad is an intended third-party beneficiary of this Section 3.4 and of Section 9.5 of this Agreement.

*Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC, et al.* Case No. 1021-00006 Circuit Court of the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County, Florida
