**SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND MUTUAL RELEASE**
This **SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND MUTUAL RELEASE** (this \"Agreement\") is entered into and made effective as of April 22, 2024 (the \"Effective Date\"), by and among the following parties:

**VERIMARK HOSPITALITY GROUP INC.**, a Delaware corporation, with its principal place of business at 2400 East Las Olas Boulevard, Suite 3100, Fort Lauderdale, Florida 33301, and whose common stock is listed on the Nasdaq Stock Market under the ticker symbol \"VHMK\" (hereinafter referred to as \"Verimark\" or \"VHG\");
and

**COASTAL PALMS FRANCHISE HOLDINGS LLC**, a Florida limited liability company, with its principal office at 9500 Gulf Shore Drive, Suite 450, Naples, Florida 34108 (hereinafter referred to as \"Coastal Palms\" or \"CPFH\");

**RANDALL \"RANDY\" BRECKER**, an individual residing in the State of Florida, who serves as the Managing Member and holds a sixty percent (60%) equity interest in Coastal Palms, and who also serves as the President of Suncoast Room Management Inc. (hereinafter referred to as \"R. Brecker\");
**THERESA BRECKER**, an individual residing in the State of Florida, who is a Member of and holds a fifteen percent (15%) equity interest in Coastal Palms (hereinafter referred to as \"T. Brecker\");

**NOLAN PRESCOTT**, an individual residing in the State of Florida, who is a Member of and holds a twenty-five percent (25%) equity interest in Coastal Palms (hereinafter referred to as \"Prescott\");
**GULF BREEZE HOSPITALITY LLC**, a Florida limited liability company (hereinafter referred to as \"Gulf Breeze\");
**SAVANNAH LODGING PARTNERS LLC**, a Georgia limited liability company (hereinafter referred to as \"Savannah Lodging\");
**SUNCOAST ROOM MANAGEMENT INC.**, a Florida corporation (hereinafter referred to as \"Suncoast\");

Coastal Palms, R. Brecker, T. Brecker, Prescott, Gulf Breeze, Savannah Lodging, and Suncoast are collectively referred to herein as the \"Coastal Palms Parties.\" Verimark and the Coastal Palms Parties are collectively referred to herein as the \"Parties\" and each individually as a \"Party.\"
**[RECITALS]{.underline}**
**WHEREAS:**

**A. Franchise Relationship.** Verimark operates and franchises approximately 340 branded hotel properties across the southeastern United States under the \"Verimark Suites,\" \"Verimark Select,\" and \"Verimark Grand\" flags. For fiscal year 2021, Verimark reported consolidated revenue of approximately \$1.42 billion, of which the franchise segment contributed approximately \$218 million. Coastal Palms is the operator of twenty-two (22) franchised hotel properties --- eighteen (18) operating under the Verimark Suites flag and four (4) operating under the Verimark Select flag --- located across the States of Florida and Georgia, comprising approximately 3,740 total guest rooms. The first Franchise License Agreement (\"FLA\") between Verimark and Coastal Palms was executed on June 15, 2007, for a Verimark Suites property located in Naples, Florida. Over the following years, Coastal Palms and its affiliates executed a total of twenty-two (22) individual FLAs with Verimark, the most recent of which was dated September 3, 2019. Each FLA provides for a twenty (20)-year initial term and is governed by the laws of the State of Florida, with mandatory venue for any disputes in Broward County, Florida. Under each FLA, Coastal Palms is required to pay the following fees: (i) a royalty equal to five percent (5%) of Gross Room Revenue (\"GRR\") (FLA § 4.1); (ii) a marketing-fund contribution equal to two and one-half percent (2.5%) of GRR (FLA § 4.2); and (iii) a technology fee of twelve dollars and fifty cents (\$12.50) per available room per month, adjusted annually for changes in the Consumer Price Index, with such adjustment capped at three percent (3%) per year (FLA § 4.3). Late-payment interest under the FLAs accrues at a rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month, compounded monthly (FLA § 4.6). Additionally, FLA § 15.3 provides for liquidated damages upon termination for cause in an amount equal to three times (3×) the trailing-twelve-month royalties per property... (line truncated to 2000 chars)

**B. The Litigation.** On November 8, 2021, a former Coastal Palms regional controller, Janet Kerrigan, reported to Verimark\'s compliance hotline allegations of systematic revenue underreporting by the Coastal Palms Parties. In response, Verimark retained Thornbury & Associates CPAs LLP to conduct a franchise-compliance audit of the Coastal Palms properties. Thornbury\'s preliminary findings, delivered to Verimark on January 18, 2022, indicated that the audited properties had underreported GRR by approximately twenty-six percent (26%) for the period spanning fiscal years 2019 through 2021. Verimark issued a Notice of Material Breach to Coastal Palms on February 4, 2022, demanding that Coastal Palms cure the identified breaches within thirty (30) days in accordance with FLA § 14.1. Coastal Palms, through its counsel Whitfield, Barrow & Crane LLP, responded by letter dated February 28, 2022, denying any material breach and contesting the methodology and conclusions of the Thornbury audit. No cure was tendered by Coastal Palms within the thirty (30)-day period, which expired on March 6, 2022. On March 7, 2022, Verimark filed a ten-count Complaint in the Circuit Court of the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County, Florida, bearing Case Number 1021-00006 (the \"Litigation\"), asserting claims for: (i) breach of contract --- royalties; (ii) breach of contract --- marketing fund; (iii) breach of contract --- technology fees; (iv) breach of the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing; (v) fraudulent concealment; (vi) negligent misrepresentation; (vii) unjust enrichment; (viii) declaratory judgment; (ix) accounting; and (x) civil conspiracy. In the Complaint, Verimark claimed damages in the approximate aggregate amount of \$150,000,000, consisting of: (a) \$16,095,000 in direct underpayments of royalties, marketing-fund contributions, and technology fees; (b) \$28,400,000 in contractual late-payment interest calculated in accordance with FLA § 4.6; a... (line truncated to 2000 chars)

**C. Summary Judgment Ruling.** On February 9, 2024, the Court (the Honorable Richard M. Calloway, Circuit Judge) entered an Order granting Verimark\'s Motion for Partial Summary Judgment on Count I (Breach of Contract --- Royalties) and Count II (Breach of Contract --- Marketing Fund), finding as a matter of law that Coastal Palms\' exclusion of revenues collected by Suncoast Room Management Inc. from its calculation and reporting of GRR constituted a material breach of FLA §§ 4.1 and 4.2. The Court denied Coastal Palms\' Cross-Motion for Summary Judgment on all counts and deferred the determination of damages to trial.

**D. Mediation and Settlement.** On February 23, 2024, the Parties agreed to submit their dispute to mediation before the Honorable Patricia Everwood (Retired), of Everwood Dispute Resolution PLLC. A two-day mediation session was conducted on March 14 and 15, 2024, at 396 Alhambra Circle, Suite 800, Coral Gables, Florida 33134. A tentative settlement was reached on the second day of mediation, March 15, 2024, and the Parties executed a written term sheet memorializing the principal terms of the settlement on March 22, 2024. The Parties now desire to fully and finally resolve all claims and counterclaims in the Litigation, and all related disputes among the Parties, on the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement.

**E. Desire to Settle.** The Parties acknowledge the uncertainty, risk, and expense inherent in continued litigation and trial, and each Party has made an independent assessment of the merits and risks of its respective claims and defenses. The Parties desire to avoid the further burden and expense of trial and to resolve their disputes amicably and in full. Entry into this Agreement is not, and shall not be construed as, an admission of liability, wrongdoing, or the validity of any claim or defense by any Party. Each Party has been represented by competent legal counsel of its choosing in the negotiation and execution of this Agreement, and each Party has had a full and fair opportunity to review, analyze, and negotiate the terms set forth herein.

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual promises, covenants, releases, and agreements set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:
**[ARTICLE I --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Article I shall have the meanings ascribed to them elsewhere in this Agreement.

**1.1** \"**Agreement**\" means this Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release, together with all Exhibits and Schedules attached hereto, which are incorporated herein by reference and made a part hereof.

**1.2** \"**Closing**\" means the consummation of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement on the Closing Date, including the execution and delivery of this Agreement by all Parties, the payment of the Initial Payment, and the execution and delivery of all ancillary documents required to be delivered at or prior to the Closing.
**1.3** \"**Closing Date**\" means April 22, 2024.

**1.4** \"**Collateral Properties**\" means the eight (8) unencumbered hotel properties identified in Schedule 3.1 hereto, which serve as collateral for the security interest granted to Verimark pursuant to Article III.

**1.5** \"**Complaint**\" means the ten-count Complaint filed by Verimark on March 7, 2022, in Case No. 1021-00006, in the Circuit Court of the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County, Florida, together with all amendments thereto.
**1.6** \"**Counterclaim**\" means the \$12,000,000 counterclaim filed by Coastal Palms on April 18, 2022, in the Litigation, asserting claims for alleged brand-standard violations and over-billing.
**1.7** \"**Court**\" means the Circuit Court of the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County, Florida.
**1.8** \"**De-Identification Deadline**\" means August 20, 2024, which is one hundred twenty (120) days from the Closing Date.

**1.9** \"**Enhanced Audit Protocol**\" means the enhanced audit and reporting requirements applicable to the Retained Properties, as set forth in Article VIII of this Agreement and as more fully described in Exhibit D attached hereto.
**1.10** \"**Event of Default**\" has the meaning set forth in Section 2.7 of this Agreement.

**1.11** \"**Existing FLAs**\" means the twenty-two (22) Franchise License Agreements between Verimark and Coastal Palms and/or its affiliates (including Gulf Breeze and Savannah Lodging), the first of which was executed on June 15, 2007, and the most recent of which was executed on September 3, 2019, governing the operation of the Properties under the Verimark Brands.

**1.12** \"**GRR**\" or \"**Gross Room Revenue**\" has the meaning ascribed to such term in Section 4.1 of each FLA, which generally includes all revenue derived from or attributable to the rental of guest rooms at the applicable Property, regardless of the method of collection, booking channel, or collecting entity.
**1.13** \"**Initial Payment**\" means the cash payment of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000) payable by Coastal Palms to Verimark at Closing in accordance with Section 2.2 of this Agreement.

**1.14** \"**Ironclad**\" means Ironclad National Bank, a national banking association, which holds first-lien mortgage loans on eighteen (18) of the twenty-two (22) Properties, with an aggregate outstanding principal balance of approximately Ninety-Four Million Dollars (\$94,000,000) as of the date hereof.

**1.15** \"**Litigation**\" means the action styled *Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC, et al.*, Case No. 1021-00006, pending in the Circuit Court of the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County, Florida, including all claims, counterclaims, cross-claims, and third-party claims asserted therein.

**1.16** \"**New FLAs**\" means the new ten (10)-year Franchise License Agreements to be executed by Verimark and the applicable Coastal Palms Party for each of the Retained Properties, substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit C.
**1.17** \"**Payment Schedule**\" means the schedule of payments set forth in Article II and as more fully described in Exhibit A attached hereto.

**1.18** \"**Personal Guaranties**\" means the individual guaranty agreements to be executed by R. Brecker and Prescott, each substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit E, pursuant to which R. Brecker and Prescott jointly and severally guarantee all obligations of the Coastal Palms Parties under this Agreement.
**1.19** \"**Properties**\" means the twenty-two (22) hotel properties operated by the Coastal Palms Parties under the Existing FLAs.

**1.20** \"**Retained Properties**\" means the eight (8) Properties identified in Section 7.1 of this Agreement and in Exhibit C that will continue to be franchised under the New FLAs, consisting of four (4) properties in Naples, Florida; two (2) properties on Marco Island, Florida; and two (2) properties in Tampa, Florida.

**1.21** \"**Security Agreement**\" means the security agreement to be executed by Coastal Palms in favor of Verimark, substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit F, granting Verimark a first-priority security interest in the Collateral Properties to secure the Structured Payments and other obligations under this Agreement.

**1.22** \"**Settlement Amount**\" means the aggregate sum of Eighty-Seven Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$87,500,000), payable by the Coastal Palms Parties to Verimark in accordance with Article II of this Agreement.

**1.23** \"**Structured Payments**\" means the eight (8) semi-annual payments of Seven Million Eight Hundred Twelve Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$7,812,500) each, totaling Sixty-Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$62,500,000), payable in accordance with Section 2.3 of this Agreement, the first such payment being due on October 22, 2024, and the last such payment being due on April 22, 2028, as more fully described in the Payment Schedule attached hereto as Exhibit A.

**1.24** \"**Surrendered Properties**\" means the fourteen (14) Properties identified in Section 7.1 and Exhibit B of this Agreement that are subject to franchise surrender, de-identification, and termination of the applicable Existing FLAs.

**1.25** \"**Verimark Brands**\" means \"Verimark Suites,\" \"Verimark Select,\" and \"Verimark Grand,\" together with all associated trademarks, service marks, logos, trade dress, proprietary systems (including reservation systems, property management systems, and revenue management systems), and all other intellectual property owned, licensed, or controlled by Verimark in connection with the branding and operation of its franchised hotel properties.
**[ARTICLE II --- SETTLEMENT PAYMENT]{.underline}**

**Section 2.1 --- Total Settlement Amount.** In full and final settlement of all claims, counterclaims, causes of action, and disputes among the Parties, whether asserted or unasserted, known or unknown, arising from or relating to the Existing FLAs, the Litigation, or the subject matter thereof, the Coastal Palms Parties shall pay to Verimark a total Settlement Amount of Eighty-Seven Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$87,500,000), payable as follows:
> \(a\) The Initial Payment of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000), payable at the Closing in accordance with Section 2.2 below; and

> \(b\) The Structured Payments totaling Sixty-Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$62,500,000), payable in eight (8) semi-annual installments of Seven Million Eight Hundred Twelve Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$7,812,500) each, in accordance with Section 2.3 below.
The Payment Schedule setting forth the dates, amounts, and interest calculations for all payments under this Article II is attached hereto as Exhibit A and incorporated herein by reference.

**Section 2.2 --- Initial Payment.** On the Closing Date, Coastal Palms shall pay to Verimark the Initial Payment of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000) by wire transfer of immediately available funds from the escrow account established at Ironclad National Bank for the purposes of this settlement to Verimark\'s designated account. Verimark shall provide Coastal Palms with complete wire-transfer instructions for the designated receiving account no later than three (3) business days prior to the Closing Date. Upon receipt of the Initial Payment, Verimark\'s counsel, Calderwood & Harkness LLP, at 110 SE 6th Street, Suite 2800, Fort Lauderdale, Florida 33301, shall promptly issue a written confirmation of receipt to counsel for the Coastal Palms Parties. The obligation to make the Initial Payment is unconditional and shall not be subject to any right of setoff, counterclaim, defense, or deduction.

**Section 2.3 --- Structured Payments.** Following the payment of the Initial Payment, Coastal Palms shall pay to Verimark the remaining Sixty-Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$62,500,000) in eight (8) equal semi-annual installments of Seven Million Eight Hundred Twelve Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$7,812,500) each, on the following schedule:
> \(a\) The first installment shall be due and payable on October 22, 2024.
> \(b\) The second installment shall be due and payable on April 22, 2025.
> \(c\) The third installment shall be due and payable on October 22, 2025.
> \(d\) The fourth installment shall be due and payable on April 22, 2026.
> \(e\) The fifth installment shall be due and payable on October 22, 2026.
> \(f\) The sixth installment shall be due and payable on April 22, 2027.
> \(g\) The seventh installment shall be due and payable on October 22, 2027.
> \(h\) The eighth and final installment shall be due and payable on April 22, 2028.

All Structured Payments shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account designated by Verimark in accordance with the wire-transfer instructions provided pursuant to Section 2.2, or to such other account as Verimark may designate in writing from time to time upon not less than ten (10) business days\' prior notice to Coastal Palms.

**Section 2.4 --- Interest on Structured Payments.** Interest shall accrue on the outstanding principal balance of the Structured Payments at a rate of six and one-half percent (6.5%) per annum, simple interest, calculated on the basis of a 365-day year and the actual number of days elapsed. Interest shall begin to accrue on the Closing Date and shall be calculated on the then-outstanding principal balance of the Structured Payments. Interest payments shall be due and payable concurrently with each semi-annual installment payment. The amount of interest due with each installment shall be calculated by multiplying the outstanding principal balance as of the first day of the applicable interest period by the annual interest rate of 6.5%, and then multiplying the result by a fraction, the numerator of which is the actual number of days elapsed during such interest period and the denominator of which is 365. A detailed schedule setting forth the estimated interest amounts due with each installment is set forth in Exhibit A.

**Section 2.5 --- Late Payments.** Any Structured Payment (including any concurrent interest payment) not received by Verimark within ten (10) business days of its scheduled due date shall bear additional default interest at the rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month on the overdue amount, calculated from the original due date until the date on which such overdue amount is received by Verimark in full. This default interest shall be in addition to, and not in substitution for, the interest otherwise payable under Section 2.4. If Coastal Palms fails to cure a late payment within thirty (30) days after written notice from Verimark specifying the overdue payment and the amount due, such failure shall constitute an Event of Default under Section 2.7 of this Agreement. Nothing in this Section 2.5 shall be construed to extend the due date for any Structured Payment or to waive Verimark\'s right to declare an Event of Default following the expiration of the applicable cure period.

**Section 2.6 --- Prepayment.** Coastal Palms may, at its option, prepay all or any portion of the Structured Payments at any time without premium, penalty, or additional charge of any kind. Any partial prepayment shall be applied first to any accrued and unpaid interest on the outstanding principal balance of the Structured Payments, and second to the scheduled installments in inverse order of maturity (i.e., applied first to the most distant scheduled installment, then to the next most distant, and so on), thereby reducing the total interest obligation over the remaining term. Coastal Palms shall provide Verimark with not less than five (5) business days\' prior written notice of any prepayment, specifying the amount and intended date of such prepayment. Verimark shall recalculate the interest amounts due on any remaining installments following any partial prepayment and shall provide an updated Payment Schedule to Coastal Palms within ten (10) business days of receipt of any such prepayment.
**Section 2.7 --- Events of Default and Acceleration.** An \"Event of Default\" shall be deemed to have occurred upon the happening of any of the following:

> \(a\) **Payment Default.** Failure by any Coastal Palms Party to make any payment of the Structured Payments, accrued interest, or any other monetary obligation under this Agreement within thirty (30) days of the date on which Verimark delivers written notice to Coastal Palms specifying such payment default;

> \(b\) **Covenant Default.** Breach by any Coastal Palms Party of any material covenant, agreement, or obligation under this Agreement (other than a payment obligation, which is governed by clause (a) above) that remains uncured for thirty (30) days after Verimark delivers written notice to Coastal Palms specifying such breach in reasonable detail;

> \(c\) **Bankruptcy or Insolvency.** The commencement of any voluntary or involuntary proceeding under the United States Bankruptcy Code, Title 11, United States Code, or under any state insolvency, receivership, dissolution, or similar statute, by or against any Coastal Palms Party, or the appointment of a receiver, trustee, custodian, or similar official for the business, assets, or property of any Coastal Palms Party, or the making of a general assignment for the benefit of creditors by any Coastal Palms Party;

> \(d\) **Breach of Representations and Warranties.** Any representation or warranty made by any Coastal Palms Party in this Agreement or in any ancillary document delivered in connection herewith that is materially inaccurate, false, or misleading as of the date on which it was made, and such inaccuracy, falsity, or misleading character is not cured within thirty (30) days after written notice from Verimark specifying the same;

> \(e\) **De-Identification Failure.** Failure by any Coastal Palms Party to comply with the de-identification requirements set forth in Article VII of this Agreement by the De-Identification Deadline.

Upon the occurrence of an Event of Default, Verimark may, at its sole election and upon written notice to Coastal Palms, declare the entire outstanding principal balance of the Structured Payments, together with all accrued and unpaid interest thereon and all other amounts owing under this Agreement, immediately due and payable in full, without further notice, demand, presentment, or protest, all of which are hereby waived by the Coastal Palms Parties. Acceleration of the Structured Payments pursuant to this Section 2.7 shall not constitute a waiver of, or limit, any other rights or remedies available to Verimark at law or in equity, including, without limitation, the right to enforce the Security Agreement, to seek collection under the Personal Guaranties, to pursue foreclosure on the Collateral Properties, and to seek injunctive or other equitable relief from the Court.

**Section 2.8 --- Tax Treatment.** Each Party shall be solely responsible for the payment of all federal, state, and local taxes, and for the filing of all tax returns and reports, arising from or attributable to the payments received or made by such Party under this Agreement. The Parties agree that, for federal and state income-tax purposes, the Settlement Amount shall be treated by all Parties as compensatory damages and that no portion of the Settlement Amount shall be characterized as punitive damages, penalties, or interest for tax purposes, except to the extent required by applicable law. The Coastal Palms Parties shall be solely responsible for any and all withholding obligations, including but not limited to any obligation to withhold and remit taxes on behalf of Verimark, if any such obligation exists under applicable law. No Party shall take any position on any tax return or in any proceeding before any taxing authority that is inconsistent with the treatment described in this Section 2.8, unless required to do so by a final determination (as defined in Section 1313(a) of the Internal Revenue Code) of a court of competent jurisdiction or an applicable taxing authority.
**[ARTICLE III --- SECURITY FOR STRUCTURED PAYMENTS]{.underline}**

**Section 3.1 --- Security Interest.** To secure the prompt and full payment and performance of all obligations of the Coastal Palms Parties under this Agreement, including, without limitation, the payment of all Structured Payments, accrued interest thereon, default interest, and any indemnification obligations arising under Article X, Coastal Palms hereby grants to Verimark a first-priority security interest in the eight (8) unencumbered hotel properties identified in Schedule 3.1 attached hereto (the \"Collateral Properties\"), together with all improvements, fixtures, furnishings, equipment, accounts, general intangibles, and proceeds related thereto (collectively, the \"Collateral\"). The aggregate appraised value of the Collateral Properties, as determined by independent appraisals conducted by licensed commercial real-estate appraisers within the ninety (90)-day period preceding the Closing Date, is not less than Seventy-One Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$71,200,000). The security interest granted hereunder shall be evidenced by the Security Agreement, which shall be substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit F and shall be executed and delivered concurrently with the execution of this Agreement.

**Section 3.2 --- UCC Filings.** To perfect the security interest granted under Section 3.1, Coastal Palms hereby authorizes Verimark, and Verimark\'s counsel, Calderwood & Harkness LLP, to prepare, execute, and file on behalf of Coastal Palms UCC-1 Financing Statements with the Florida Secured Transaction Registry and with any other filing office in any jurisdiction where filing may be necessary or advisable to perfect or maintain Verimark\'s security interest in the Collateral. The UCC-1 Financing Statement shall identify the following:
> **Debtor:** Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC, 9500 Gulf Shore Drive, Suite 450, Naples, Florida 34108

23: **[I. PURPOSE AND SCOPE OF MEMORANDUM]{.underline}**

25: The purpose of this memorandum is to memorialize the final disposition of the above-referenced matter, provide a comprehensive summary of the engagement from inception through closing, document the financial outcomes of the litigation --- including fees, costs, and the terms of the settlement achieved on behalf of the client --- capture key learnings and practice points for the benefit of the firm, and establish file-retention instructions in accordance with Calderwood & Harkness LLP\'s Document Retention Policy. This memorandum is intended to serve as the definitive internal record of the matter for future reference by firm attorneys, the conflicts department, and firm management.

33: **[A. Client and Parties]{.underline}**
34: 
35: **1. Client. Verimark Hospitality Group Inc.** (\"Verimark\" or \"VHG\") is a Delaware corporation publicly traded on the Nasdaq Stock Market under the ticker symbol VHMK. Verimark is headquartered at 2400 East Las Olas Boulevard, Suite 3100, Fort Lauderdale, Florida 33301. For fiscal year 2021 --- the most recent full fiscal year preceding the commencement of this litigation --- Verimark reported consolidated revenue of approximately \$1.42 billion, of which its franchise segment contributed approximately \$218 million. Verimark operates and franchises approximately 340 branded hotel properties under three primary flags --- Verimark Suites, Verimark Select, and Verimark Grand --- located predominantly across the southeastern United States.
36: 
37: The following individuals served as the firm\'s primary client contacts throughout the engagement:
38: 
39: > • **Renata Solis-Vega**, Senior Vice President and General Counsel --- principal point of contact for all legal strategy, settlement authority, and privilege-related matters.

41: > • **Martin Holcomb**, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer --- primary contact for financial matters, fee and cost approvals, budget discussions, and settlement economics.

43: > • **Deidre Langston**, Senior Vice President, Franchise Operations --- primary contact for operational matters, franchise compliance, property-level data, and post-settlement monitoring of franchise-surrender and enhanced-audit obligations.
44: 
45: **2. Defendants.** The following parties were named as defendants in this action:
46: 
47: **(a) Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC** (\"Coastal Palms\" or \"CPFH\") --- a Florida limited liability company with its principal office at 9500 Gulf Shore Drive, Suite 450, Naples, Florida 34108. Coastal Palms\' registered agent is Garrison Registered Agents LLC, 100 S. Ashley Drive, Suite 600, Tampa, Florida 33602. Coastal Palms was, at the time of the filing of this action, Verimark\'s single largest franchise operator, holding franchise rights to twenty-two (22) hotel properties --- eighteen (18) operating under the Verimark Suites flag and four (4) operating under the Verimark Select flag --- located across Florida and Georgia, comprising approximately 3,740 total guest rooms.
48: 
49: **(b) Randall \"Randy\" Brecker** --- Managing Member and sixty percent (60%) equity holder of Coastal Palms. Mr. Brecker served as the day-to-day decision-maker for all Coastal Palms operations and was also the President of Suncoast Room Management Inc., the affiliated management company through which the revenue-diversion scheme was conducted.
50: 
51: **(c) Theresa Brecker** --- Member and fifteen percent (15%) equity holder of Coastal Palms. Ms. Brecker is the spouse of Randall Brecker. Her involvement in the day-to-day operations of Coastal Palms was limited, but she was a signatory on certain financial documents and loan agreements relevant to the litigation.
52: 
53: **(d) Nolan Prescott** --- Member and twenty-five percent (25%) equity holder of Coastal Palms. Mr. Prescott is a retired commercial real estate developer who served as a passive investor in Coastal Palms. His role was principally financial; he did not participate in day-to-day management but was a co-guarantor on several of the Ironclad National Bank mortgage loans and was a signatory on the operating agreement.
54: 
55: **(e) Gulf Breeze Hospitality LLC** --- a Florida limited liability company owning and operating six (6) Verimark Suites properties in Southwest Florida. Gulf Breeze Hospitality LLC was managed by Randall Brecker and functioned as a subsidiary or affiliate entity within the Coastal Palms organizational structure.
56: 
57: **(f) Savannah Lodging Partners LLC** --- a Georgia limited liability company owning and operating four (4) Verimark Suites properties in coastal Georgia (Savannah and Brunswick). Savannah Lodging Partners LLC was likewise managed by Randall Brecker.
58: 
59: **(g) Suncoast Room Management Inc.** --- a Florida corporation; an affiliated management company established by Randall Brecker no later than January 2013. Suncoast collected revenues from direct bookings --- including walk-in guests, corporate-direct contracts, and bookings made through the unbranded website gulfcoastrooms.com --- and retained a twelve percent (12%) \"management fee\" on those revenues. Neither Suncoast\'s gross collections nor the management fee were included in the Gross Room Revenue reports submitted to Verimark. Suncoast was the central vehicle through which the revenue-diversion scheme operated.
60: 
61: **3. Defense Counsel**
62: 
63: Coastal Palms and all individual and entity defendants were jointly represented by **Whitfield, Barrow & Crane LLP** (\"WBC\"), 1221 Brickell Avenue, Suite 3000, Miami, Florida 33131. The defense team was led by:
64: 
65: > • **Nathan Whitfield III**, Senior Partner --- lead trial counsel.
66: >
67: > • **Gabriela Montes**, Partner --- responsible for discovery and motions practice.
68: >
69: > • **Ethan Doyle**, Associate --- supporting research, briefing, and deposition preparation.
70: 
71: **[B. Nature of the Dispute]{.underline}**
72: 
73: This matter involved a breach-of-contract action arising from Coastal Palms\' systematic underreporting of Gross Room Revenue (\"GRR\") over a nine-year period spanning 2013 through 2021. The underreporting resulted in the chronic and substantial underpayment of three categories of fees owed to Verimark under the parties\' Franchise License Agreements: (i) royalties, calculated at five percent (5%) of GRR pursuant to FLA § 4.1; (ii) marketing-fund contributions, calculated at two and one-half percent (2.5%) of GRR pursuant to FLA § 4.2; and (iii) technology fees, assessed at \$12.50 per available room per month, with consumer price index adjustments capped at three percent (3%) annually, pursuant to FLA § 4.3.
74: 
75: The revenue-diversion scheme at the heart of this dispute operated as follows: Beginning no later than January 2013, Coastal Palms, acting through and at the direction of Randall Brecker, established Suncoast Room Management Inc. as a nominally separate management company. Suncoast collected revenues from direct bookings --- a category encompassing walk-in guests paying at the front desk, corporate accounts that booked directly with the properties rather than through Verimark\'s centralized reservation system, and guests who booked through the unbranded website gulfcoastrooms.com, which Suncoast created and operated. Suncoast retained a twelve percent (12%) \"management fee\" on all revenues it collected. Critically, neither Suncoast\'s gross collections nor the management fee were included in the GRR figures that Coastal Palms reported to Verimark for purposes of calculating royalties, marketing-fund contributions, and technology fees.
76: 
77: In addition to the Suncoast-based diversion, Coastal Palms also systematically underreported revenue from third-party online travel agencies (\"OTAs\") by netting commissions paid to the OTAs against GRR before reporting it to Verimark. This netting practice violated the FLAs\' definition of GRR, which was defined on a gross basis without deduction for commissions, discounts, or fees paid to intermediaries.
78: 
79: The underreporting was estimated at between twenty-two percent (22%) and thirty-one percent (31%) of actual GRR across the portfolio, with variation by individual property and by year. The total underreported GRR over the nine-year period was estimated at approximately \$197.8 million. For fiscal year 2021 alone --- the year immediately preceding the discovery of the scheme --- Coastal Palms reported GRR of \$112.4 million, whereas estimated true GRR was \$145.6 million, representing an underreporting of approximately \$33.2 million for that single year.
80:

The first FLA was executed on June 15, 2007, for the Naples property, and the most recent FLA was executed on September 3, 2019. Each FLA provided for a twenty (20)-year initial term and was governed by the laws of the State of Florida, with mandatory venue for any litigation in Broward County, Florida.

131: **[A. Pre-Litigation Phase (November 2021 -- March 2022)]{.underline}**
132: 
133: The origins of this matter trace to a whistleblower complaint received by Verimark\'s compliance hotline. On **November 8, 2021**, Janet Kerrigan, a former regional controller for Coastal Palms who had been terminated in October 2021, contacted the Verimark compliance hotline and reported allegations of systematic revenue diversion by Coastal Palms and its affiliated entity, Suncoast Room Management Inc. Ms. Kerrigan alleged that Randall Brecker had directed property-level accounting staff to exclude direct-booking revenues collected by Suncoast from the GRR reports submitted to Verimark, and that this practice had been ongoing for several years.
134: 
135: On **November 15, 2021**, Calderwood & Harkness LLP, operating under a separate pre-engagement letter agreement with Verimark for advisory services, provided a preliminary analysis of the whistleblower allegations. Yuki Nakamura prepared a memorandum to Priya Anand assessing the legal implications of the allegations under the FLAs, the potential scope of damages, and the recommended investigative steps. The memorandum concluded that, if substantiated, the allegations described conduct that would constitute both a material breach and a potentially incurable breach under FLA § 14.2(c).
136: 
137: On **November 22, 2021**, Verimark engaged **Thornbury & Associates CPAs LLP** (lead audit partner: Malcolm Thornbury, CPA; principal office: 1551 N. Flagler Drive, Suite 800, West Palm Beach, Florida 33401) to conduct a franchise-compliance audit of Coastal Palms\' ten (10) highest-grossing properties pursuant to the audit-rights provisions of FLA § 8.2. The audit scope covered fiscal years 2019 through 2021 and was designed to test the accuracy of GRR reporting against available bank records, OTA statements, and property-management system data.
138: 
139: On **January 18, 2022**, Thornbury delivered its preliminary findings. The audit revealed that the ten (10) audited properties had underreported GRR by approximately twenty-six percent (26%) for the period 2019--2021. Extrapolation of these findings across all twenty-two (22) Coastal Palms properties and the full nine-year period of 2013--2021 yielded an estimated \$197.8 million in total underreported GRR. These preliminary findings confirmed the substance of Ms. Kerrigan\'s whistleblower allegations and provided the evidentiary foundation for the pre-suit demand and the subsequent litigation.

WBC further contended that Verimark had been aware of Suncoast\'s role because Suncoast was identified in property-management agreements submitted during the franchise-application process.

**[B. Nature of the Dispute]{.underline}**

This matter involved a breach-of-contract action arising from Coastal Palms\' systematic underreporting of Gross Room Revenue (\"GRR\") over a nine-year period spanning 2013 through 2021. The underreporting resulted in the chronic and substantial underpayment of three categories of fees owed to Verimark under the parties\' Franchise License Agreements: (i) royalties, calculated at five percent (5%) of GRR pursuant to FLA § 4.1; (ii) marketing-fund contributions, calculated at two and one-half percent (2.5%) of GRR pursuant to FLA § 4.2; and (iii) technology fees, assessed at \$12.50 per available room per month, with consumer price index adjustments capped at three percent (3%) annually, pursuant to FLA § 4.3.

The revenue-diversion scheme at the heart of this dispute operated as follows: Beginning no later than January 2013, Coastal Palms, acting through and at the direction of Randall Brecker, established Suncoast Room Management Inc. as a nominally separate management company. Suncoast collected revenues from direct bookings --- a category encompassing walk-in guests paying at the front desk, corporate accounts that booked directly with the properties rather than through Verimark\'s centralized reservation system, and guests who booked through the unbranded website gulfcoastrooms.com, which Suncoast created and operated. Suncoast retained a twelve percent (12%) \"management fee\" on all revenues it collected. Critically, neither Suncoast\'s gross collections nor the management fee were included in the GRR figures that Coastal Palms reported to Verimark for purposes of calculating royalties, marketing-fund contributions, and technology fees.

In addition to the Suncoast-based diversion, Coastal Palms also systematically underreported revenue from third-party online travel agencies (\"OTAs\") by netting commissions paid to the OTAs against GRR before reporting it to Verimark. This netting practice violated the FLAs\' definition of GRR, which was defined on a gross basis without deduction for commissions, discounts, or fees paid to intermediaries.

The underreporting was estimated at between twenty-two percent (22%) and thirty-one percent (31%) of actual GRR across the portfolio, with variation by individual property and by year. The total underreported GRR over the nine-year period was estimated at approximately \$197.8 million. For fiscal year 2021 alone --- the year immediately preceding the discovery of the scheme --- Coastal Palms reported GRR of \$112.4 million, whereas estimated true GRR was \$145.6 million, representing an underreporting of approximately \$33.2 million for that single year.
**[C. Franchise License Agreements]{.underline}**

The contractual relationship between Verimark and Coastal Palms was governed by twenty-two (22) individual Franchise License Agreements (\"FLAs\"), one for each franchised hotel property. The first FLA was executed on June 15, 2007, for the Naples property, and the most recent FLA was executed on September 3, 2019. Each FLA provided for a twenty (20)-year initial term and was governed by the laws of the State of Florida, with mandatory venue for any litigation in Broward County, Florida.
The following provisions of the FLAs were of central importance to the claims asserted in this matter:

> • **Section 4.1 --- Royalties:** Franchisee to pay Verimark a royalty equal to five percent (5%) of Gross Room Revenue, payable monthly, within fifteen (15) days following the end of each calendar month.

> • **Section 4.2 --- Marketing-Fund Contribution:** Franchisee to contribute two and one-half percent (2.5%) of Gross Room Revenue to the Verimark National Marketing Fund, payable concurrently with royalties.

> • **Section 4.3 --- Technology Fee:** Franchisee to pay a technology fee of \$12.50 per available room per month, subject to annual CPI adjustment capped at three percent (3%) per year, to support Verimark\'s centralized reservation system, property-management system integrations, and brand technology platforms.
> • **Section 4.6 --- Late-Payment Interest:** Any amounts not paid when due to bear interest at a rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month, compounded monthly, until paid in full.

> • **Section 8.2 --- Audit Rights:** Verimark entitled to audit franchisee\'s financial records upon ten (10) business days\' written notice. If an audit reveals an underpayment exceeding two percent (2%) of reported GRR for the audited period, the franchisee bears all audit costs.

These provisions collectively formed the legal framework upon which Verimark\'s claims were built and provided the contractual bases for the damages calculations set forth in Dr. Kettlewell\'s expert report.
**[D. Court and Case Information]{.underline}**
> • **Court:** Circuit Court of the 17th Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County, Florida.
> • **Assigned Judge:** Honorable Richard M. Calloway, Circuit Judge.

The Court\'s handling of the matter was efficient and well-managed, with the most significant judicial intervention being the Court\'s October 28, 2022 Order granting the Motion to Compel and the February 9, 2024 Order granting Verimark\'s Motion for Partial Summary Judgment on Counts I and II.
**[E. Calderwood & Harkness Engagement Team]{.underline}**
The following attorneys and staff comprised the Calderwood & Harkness LLP engagement team for this matter:

> • **Priya Anand** --- Responsible Partner, Litigation (General); Florida Bar No. 0087451. Ms. Anand has twenty-two (22) years of experience in complex commercial litigation and franchise disputes and served as the lead strategist and trial counsel for Verimark throughout the engagement. Ms. Anand was responsible for all significant strategic decisions, client communications, settlement negotiations, and the mediation.

> • **Douglas Carmichael** --- Billing Partner, Litigation (General); Florida Bar No. 0093217. Mr. Carmichael has nineteen (19) years of experience and served as co-counsel on the matter, with primary responsibility for billing, budget management, and client reporting on financial matters. Mr. Carmichael also participated in the summary-judgment briefing and mediation.

> • **Yuki Nakamura** --- Lead Associate, Litigation (General); Florida Bar No. 0119644. Ms. Nakamura has seven (7) years of experience and managed the day-to-day conduct of the litigation, including oversight of discovery, coordination with the e-discovery vendor (Nexagen Document Solutions LLC), preparation of deposition outlines, drafting of significant portions of the summary-judgment briefing, and coordination with expert witnesses. Ms. Nakamura was the primary drafter of the confidential mediation statement and the settlement agreement.

> • **Carlos Espinoza** --- Working Associate, Litigation (General); Florida Bar No. 0128903. Mr. Espinoza has four (4) years of experience and provided substantial support on deposition preparation, damages analysis coordination with the forensic expert, research memoranda on franchise-law issues, and drafting of discovery correspondence and motions.

> • **Additional Timekeepers:** Approximately 1,250 hours of work were performed by paralegals and contract attorneys at a blended rate of approximately \$285 per hour. This work included document review during the discovery phase, deposition logistics, cite-checking of briefs, and administrative support for the mediation and settlement process.
**[III. ENGAGEMENT HISTORY AND KEY MILESTONES]{.underline}**
**[A. Pre-Litigation Phase (November 2021 -- March 2022)]{.underline}**

The origins of this matter trace to a whistleblower complaint received by Verimark\'s compliance hotline. On **November 8, 2021**, Janet Kerrigan, a former regional controller for Coastal Palms who had been terminated in October 2021, contacted the Verimark compliance hotline and reported allegations of systematic revenue diversion by Coastal Palms and its affiliated entity, Suncoast Room Management Inc. Ms. Kerrigan alleged that Randall Brecker had directed property-level accounting staff to exclude direct-booking revenues collected by Suncoast from the GRR reports submitted to Verimark, and that this practice had been ongoing for several years.

On **November 15, 2021**, Calderwood & Harkness LLP, operating under a separate pre-engagement letter agreement with Verimark for advisory services, provided a preliminary analysis of the whistleblower allegations. Yuki Nakamura prepared a memorandum to Priya Anand assessing the legal implications of the allegations under the FLAs, the potential scope of damages, and the recommended investigative steps. The memorandum concluded that, if substantiated, the allegations described conduct that would constitute both a material breach and a potentially incurable breach under FLA § 14.2(c).

On **November 22, 2021**, Verimark engaged **Thornbury & Associates CPAs LLP** (lead audit partner: Malcolm Thornbury, CPA; principal office: 1551 N. Flagler Drive, Suite 800, West Palm Beach, Florida 33401) to conduct a franchise-compliance audit of Coastal Palms\' ten (10) highest-grossing properties pursuant to the audit-rights provisions of FLA § 8.2. The audit scope covered fiscal years 2019 through 2021 and was designed to test the accuracy of GRR reporting against available bank records, OTA statements, and property-management system data.

On **January 18, 2022**, Thornbury delivered its preliminary findings. The audit revealed that the ten (10) audited properties had underreported GRR by approximately twenty-six percent (26%) for the period 2019--2021. Extrapolation of these findings across all twenty-two (22) Coastal Palms properties and the full nine-year period of 2013--2021 yielded an estimated \$197.8 million in total underreported GRR. These preliminary findings confirmed the substance of Ms. Kerrigan\'s whistleblower allegations and provided the evidentiary foundation for the pre-suit demand and the subsequent litigation.

On **February 4, 2022**, Verimark issued a formal Notice of Material Breach to Coastal Palms under FLA § 14.1, demanding that Coastal Palms cure the breach within thirty (30) days by, among other things, providing a full accounting of all revenues collected by Suncoast Room Management Inc. and remitting all underpaid royalties, marketing-fund contributions, and technology fees, together with applicable late-payment interest. Concurrently, Priya Anand transmitted a companion pre-suit demand letter to Nathan Whitfield III of WBC, advising that Calderwood & Harkness LLP had been engaged to pursue Verimark\'s claims and that litigation would follow if the breach was not cured within the cure period.

On **February 28, 2022**, WBC responded on behalf of Coastal Palms, denying any material breach. WBC asserted that Suncoast\'s revenues were properly excluded from GRR under what WBC characterized as a \"reasonable interpretation\" of the FLA\'s GRR definition, arguing that revenues collected by a separate management entity fell outside the scope of \"Gross Room Revenue\" as defined in the FLAs. WBC further contended that Verimark had been aware of Suncoast\'s role because Suncoast was identified in property-management agreements submitted during the franchise-application process.

On **March 6, 2022**, the thirty (30)-day cure period expired without any cure being tendered by Coastal Palms. At this juncture, Verimark authorized Calderwood & Harkness LLP to proceed with the filing of a breach-of-contract action.
**[B. Litigation Phase (March 2022 -- February 2024)]{.underline}**
**1. Initiation of Litigation**

On **March 4, 2022**, the formal engagement letter for litigation services was executed between Verimark and Calderwood & Harkness LLP, formally retaining the firm to prosecute the breach-of-contract action and related claims.

On **March 7, 2022**, Calderwood & Harkness LLP filed the Complaint in the Circuit Court of the 17th Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County, Florida, initiating Case No. 1021-00006. The Complaint set forth ten (10) counts:
> • **Count I** --- Breach of Contract (Royalties)
> • **Count II** --- Breach of Contract (Marketing Fund Contributions)
> • **Count III** --- Breach of Contract (Technology Fees)
> • **Count IV** --- Breach of the Implied Covenant of Good Faith and Fair Dealing
> • **Count V** --- Fraudulent Concealment
> • **Count VI** --- Negligent Misrepresentation
> • **Count VII** --- Unjust Enrichment (pleaded in the alternative)
> • **Count VIII** --- Declaratory Judgment (FLA Termination Rights)
> • **Count IX** --- Accounting
> • **Count X** --- Civil Conspiracy (against Randall Brecker and Suncoast Room Management Inc.)
Total claimed damages were approximately \$150 million, as further detailed in Section V of this memorandum.
On **March 14, 2022**, insurance coverage notification was sent to **Pinnacle Indemnity Insurance Co.** (Arthur Baines, Claims Counsel), referencing Policy No. PLI-VHG-2021-08874.
**2. Responsive Pleadings**

On **April 18, 2022**, Coastal Palms, through WBC, filed its Answer, Affirmative Defenses, and Counterclaim. The Answer denied all material allegations and asserted numerous affirmative defenses, including waiver, estoppel, laches, and ambiguity of the GRR definition. The Counterclaim sought \$12 million in damages for alleged brand-standard violations and over-billing by Verimark, contending that Verimark had failed to maintain adequate brand standards at properties outside the Coastal Palms portfolio, thereby diminishing the value of the Verimark brand and harming Coastal Palms\' properties.
On **May 2, 2022**, Verimark filed its Answer to the Counterclaim, denying all material allegations and asserting affirmative defenses.
**3. Case Management and discovery**

On **June 14, 2022**, the initial Case Management Conference was held before Judge Calloway. The Court set the matter for trial in February 2024 and established a discovery schedule with fact-discovery closing in August 2023.

On **June 20, 2022**, the parties filed a Joint Stipulation regarding the E-discovery Protocol, establishing procedures for the identification, preservation, collection, processing, review, and production of electronically stored information (\"ESI\"). **Nexagen Document Solutions LLC** (400 Northpark Town Center, Suite 500, Atlanta, Georgia 30328) was engaged by Verimark as its e-discovery vendor for document processing, hosting, and analytics.

On **July 11, 2022**, Verimark served its first set of discovery, consisting of twenty-five (25) interrogatories and one hundred forty-seven (147) requests for production directed to Coastal Palms, as well as fifteen (15) interrogatories directed to Randall Brecker individually.

On **August 8, 2022**, a subpoena duces tecum was served on **Ironclad National Bank** (Devon Schultz, Senior Vice President, at 225 Peachtree Street NE, Suite 2600, Atlanta, Georgia 30303), seeking loan documents and financial statements submitted by Coastal Palms in connection with Ironclad\'s approximately \$94 million in first-lien mortgage loans on eighteen (18) of the twenty-two (22) Coastal Palms properties. The financial statements submitted to Ironclad were expected to --- and ultimately did --- reflect the true revenue figures, creating a critical inconsistency with the GRR reports submitted to Verimark.

On **August 30, 2022**, Calderwood & Harkness LLP transmitted a detailed deficiency letter identifying twenty-three (23) categories of documents that were either missing entirely or incomplete, with particular emphasis on the absence of Suncoast Room Management Inc. financial records, gulfcoastrooms.com booking data, and bank statements for accounts maintained in Suncoast\'s name.

On **September 8, 2022**, Calderwood & Harkness LLP sent a formal meet-and-confer letter to WBC regarding the deficient production, specifically demanding production of all Suncoast Room Management Inc. records. WBC responded by asserting that Suncoast was a separate entity not subject to the discovery requests directed to Coastal Palms, notwithstanding that Suncoast was a named defendant in the action and was managed and controlled by Randall Brecker, the Managing Member of Coastal Palms.

On **September 15, 2022**, having been unable to resolve the dispute through the meet-and-confer process, Verimark filed a Motion to Compel Production of Suncoast Room Management Inc. Records. The motion was supported by a memorandum of law addressing the alter-ego and common-control doctrines and the relevance of the Suncoast records to the damages analysis.

On **October 28, 2022**, the Court granted Verimark\'s Motion to Compel, ordering Coastal Palms and Suncoast to produce all responsive documents within twenty-one (21) days. The Court found that the records sought were clearly within the control of the defendants and were directly relevant to the claims at issue.

On **November 18, 2022**, Coastal Palms made a supplemental production consisting of approximately 312,000 additional documents, including the Suncoast Room Management Inc. financial records that had been the subject of the Motion to Compel. The total volume of data processed on Verimark\'s side reached approximately 2.3 million documents comprising approximately 1.1 terabytes of data.

On **November 28, 2022**, Verimark served its Second Request for Production, consisting of thirty-four (34) requests targeting Suncoast financial data, OTA contracts, and gulfcoastrooms.com booking logs in greater detail.
**5. Expert Retention and Reports**

On **December 12, 2022**, Calderwood & Harkness LLP retained **Ridgeline Forensic Advisory LLC** (Dr. Sharon Kettlewell, CPA/CFF, CFE; principal office: 200 S. Biscayne Boulevard, Suite 1400, Miami, Florida 33131) as Verimark\'s damages expert. Dr. Kettlewell\'s engagement rates were \$475 per hour for principal-level work and \$325 per hour for staff-level support.
On **April 14, 2023**, Verimark served the expert report of Dr. Kettlewell. The report quantified the following damages:
> • Underreported GRR: \$197.8 million
> • Direct underpayments: \$16.095 million (comprising \$9.89 million in royalties, \$4.945 million in marketing-fund contributions, and \$1.26 million in technology fees)
> • Contractual late-payment interest: \$28.4 million
> • Liquidated damages under FLA § 15.3: \$105.5 million

On **May 15, 2023**, Coastal Palms served the expert report of **Prof. Grant Hargrove, PhD, CPA**, of Hargrove Economic Consulting Inc., who opined that the maximum underpayment was \$6.2 million under a narrowed definition of GRR that excluded walk-in cash payments and attributed only net OTA revenue to the franchisee.
On **June 9, 2023**, Verimark served the rebuttal expert report of Dr. Kettlewell, which addressed and refuted Prof. Hargrove\'s methodology and conclusions.
On **June 26--27, 2023**, the expert depositions of Dr. Kettlewell and Prof. Hargrove were conducted.
**6. Fact Depositions**
Between **January 9 and March 17, 2023**, the parties conducted fourteen (14) fact depositions. The key deponents and their significance were as follows:

> • **Randall Brecker** --- deposed over two (2) days, totaling fourteen (14) hours. Mr. Brecker\'s testimony was central to establishing the intent and mechanics of the revenue-diversion scheme. He acknowledged directing Suncoast to collect direct-booking revenues but maintained that the exclusion of those revenues from GRR was based on a good-faith interpretation of the FLA.
> • **Theresa Brecker** --- deposed regarding her knowledge of Coastal Palms\' financial reporting and her role as a signatory on financial documents.
> • **Nolan Prescott** --- deposed regarding his knowledge of the Suncoast arrangement and his role as a passive investor.

> • **Janet Kerrigan** --- deposed regarding her whistleblower allegations, her knowledge of the revenue-diversion scheme, and the specific instructions she received from Randall Brecker regarding the exclusion of Suncoast revenues from GRR reports.

A total of eight (8) installments plus associated interest will be due over the four-year payment period.

The ten-year retention period from matter closing (through April 26, 2034) adequately covers the entirety of the structured-payment period and extends well beyond the final payment date, ensuring that file materials remain available in the event of any enforcement action or dispute arising under the Settlement Agreement.

lines.text: On **March 8, 2024**, Verimark submitted its Confidential Mediation Statement to Mediator Everwood. The statement was twenty-eight (28) pages in length and set forth the factual background, procedural history, the significance of the Court\'s summary-judgment ruling, the damages analysis, and Verimark\'s settlement range of \$80 million to \$110 million.

On **March 11, 2024**, Calderwood & Harkness LLP transmitted a Settlement Authority Memorandum to Renata Solis-Vega and Martin Holcomb. The memorandum recommended that Verimark authorize a settlement range of \$75 million to \$95 million, based on a comprehensive risk analysis that considered the following factors: (a) the Court\'s deferral of damages quantification to trial, which left uncertainty regarding the Court\'s or jury\'s receptivity to the various damages components; (b) litigation-cost exposure, with an estimated \$1.5 million to \$2.5 million in additional fees and costs through trial; (c) a probability-weighted damages model assigning varying probabilities of success to each damages category; and (d) significant collectibility concerns arising from Ironclad National Bank\'s approximately \$94 million in first-lien mortgage loans on eighteen (18) of the twenty-two (22) Coastal Palms properties, which would take priority over any judgment Verimark obtained.
**3. Mediation Sessions**
On **March 14--15, 2024**, a two-day mediation was conducted at Everwood Dispute Resolution\'s offices in Coral Gables, Florida.

**Day 1 (March 14, 2024):** Following opening statements in joint session and an extended caucus, Coastal Palms opened with a settlement offer of \$32 million. Verimark opened with a demand of \$110 million. Through several rounds of proposals and counterproposals facilitated by Judge Everwood, the parties narrowed the gap but did not reach agreement on Day 1.

**Day 2 (March 15, 2024):** Negotiations resumed in the morning. After extensive caucuses and Mediator Everwood\'s assessment of the strengths and weaknesses of each side\'s position, a tentative agreement was reached at **\$87.5 million**, with a franchise-surrender component covering fourteen (14) of the twenty-two (22) properties. The essential terms of the settlement --- including the payment structure, security provisions, and franchise-surrender obligations --- were outlined in a mediator\'s proposal accepted by both parties.
**4. Settlement Documentation and Execution**

On **March 22, 2024**, the parties executed an eight (8)-page Settlement Term Sheet memorializing the principal terms of the agreement reached at mediation. The Term Sheet was designated as non-binding except for the exclusivity and confidentiality provisions, which were binding upon execution.

On **April 2, 2024**, Calderwood & Harkness LLP circulated to WBC the initial draft of the Settlement Agreement (Version 1, 47 pages), prepared principally by Yuki Nakamura under the supervision of Priya Anand.

On **April 10, 2024**, WBC returned a redline (Version 2) with Coastal Palms\' proposed revisions. Calderwood & Harkness LLP prepared marginal comments and a drafting issues memorandum identifying areas requiring further negotiation.

On **April 22, 2024**, the **Final Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release (Execution Version, 52 pages)** was fully executed by all parties: Verimark Hospitality Group Inc., Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC, Randall Brecker, Theresa Brecker, Nolan Prescott, Gulf Breeze Hospitality LLC, Savannah Lodging Partners LLC, and Suncoast Room Management Inc. The \$25 million cash payment at closing was funded by wire transfer from an Ironclad National Bank escrow account on the same date.

On **April 26, 2024**, the **Joint Stipulation of Dismissal with Prejudice** was filed with the Court and entered by Judge Calloway, formally concluding Case No. 1021-00006. The matter was closed as of this date.
**[IV. FINAL DISPOSITION --- SETTLEMENT TERMS SUMMARY]{.underline}**

The following is a summary of the material terms of the Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release executed on April 22, 2024. This summary is provided for internal reference purposes only and is not a substitute for the full text of the Settlement Agreement, which is maintained in the matter file.
**[A. Total Settlement Amount]{.underline}**
The total settlement amount is **\$87.5 million**.
**[B. Payment Structure]{.underline}**
The \$87.5 million settlement is structured as follows:

> • **Cash Payment at Closing (April 22, 2024):** Twenty-five million dollars (\$25,000,000), funded by wire transfer from an Ironclad National Bank escrow account to Verimark\'s designated account on the date of execution.

> • **Structured Payments:** Sixty-two million five hundred thousand dollars (\$62,500,000), payable in eight (8) semi-annual installments of seven million eight hundred twelve thousand five hundred dollars (\$7,812,500) each, commencing on October 22, 2024, and continuing every six (6) months thereafter, with the final installment due on April 22, 2028.

> • **Interest on Deferred Payments:** Six and one-half percent (6.5%) per annum, simple interest, calculated on the outstanding balance of the structured payments. Interest is payable concurrently with each semi-annual installment.
**[C. Security for Structured Payments]{.underline}**
The structured-payment obligation is secured by the following:

> • **First-Priority Lien:** A first-priority security interest in eight (8) unencumbered hotel properties owned by Coastal Palms and its affiliates, with an aggregate appraised value of \$71.2 million. A UCC-1 Financing Statement has been filed with the Florida Secured Transaction Registry, identifying Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC as the debtor and Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. as the secured party.

> • **Personal Guaranties:** Randall Brecker and Nolan Prescott have each executed personal guaranties of Coastal Palms\' payment obligations under the Settlement Agreement, providing additional recovery backstops in the event of default.
**[D. Franchise Surrender]{.underline}**

Coastal Palms is required to surrender franchise rights to fourteen (14) of the twenty-two (22) franchised hotel properties within one hundred twenty (120) days of the execution of the Settlement Agreement --- that is, by **August 20, 2024**. The fourteen (14) surrendered properties are located as follows:
> • Sarasota, Florida: 3 properties
> • Fort Myers, Florida: 4 properties
> • Jacksonville, Florida: 2 properties
> • Savannah, Georgia: 3 properties
> • Brunswick, Georgia: 2 properties

De-identification requirements include the complete removal of all Verimark branding, signage, proprietary systems, and technology integrations from the surrendered properties within the 120-day deadline. A detailed de-identification checklist is attached to the Settlement Agreement as part of the franchise-surrender provisions.
**[E. Retained Properties]{.underline}**
Eight (8) properties are retained by Coastal Palms under new ten (10)-year Franchise License Agreements with enhanced audit and reporting requirements. The retained properties are located as follows:
> • Naples, Florida: 4 properties
> • Marco Island, Florida: 2 properties
> • Tampa, Florida: 2 properties

The new FLAs incorporate an **Enhanced Audit Protocol** that includes: (i) quarterly (rather than annual) franchise-compliance audits; (ii) real-time point-of-sale (\"POS\") integration with Verimark\'s centralized revenue-management system, providing Verimark with continuous access to revenue data; and (iii) Coastal Palms bearing all audit costs for a period of five (5) years from the effective date of the new FLAs.
**[F. Counterclaim Dismissal]{.underline}**
Coastal Palms dismissed its \$12 million counterclaim with prejudice as part of the settlement, without any payment or concession by Verimark.
**[G. Mutual Release]{.underline}**

The Settlement Agreement contains a broad mutual release of all claims arising from or related to the FLAs through the effective date of the Settlement Agreement, with the sole exception of obligations arising under the Settlement Agreement itself, the new FLAs, and the related security instruments.
**[H. Confidentiality and Non-Disparagement]{.underline}**

The settlement amount and terms are subject to confidentiality restrictions, with an exception for Verimark\'s disclosure obligations under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. Verimark disclosed the settlement as a \"material litigation settlement\" in its Q2 2024 Form 10-Q filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. The Settlement Agreement also contains a mutual non-disparagement clause with a three (3)-year term.
**[I. Settlement Agreement Exhibits]{.underline}**
The Settlement Agreement includes the following exhibits:
> • **Exhibit A:** Payment Schedule
> • **Exhibit B:** List of Surrendered Properties (14 properties)
> • **Exhibit C:** Form of New Franchise License Agreements for Retained Properties (8 properties)

**A. Franchise Relationship.** Verimark operates and franchises approximately 340 branded hotel properties across the southeastern United States under the \"Verimark Suites,\" \"Verimark Select,\" and \"Verimark Grand\" flags. For fiscal year 2021, Verimark reported consolidated revenue of approximately \$1.42 billion, of which the franchise segment contributed approximately \$218 million. Coastal Palms is the operator of twenty-two (22) franchised hotel properties --- eighteen (18) operating under the Verimark Suites flag and four (4) operating under the Verimark Select flag --- located across the States of Florida and Georgia, comprising approximately 3,740 total guest rooms. The first Franchise License Agreement (\"FLA\") between Verimark and Coastal Palms was executed on June 15, 2007, for a Verimark Suites property located in Naples, Florida. Over the following years, Coastal Palms and its affiliates executed a total of twenty-two (22) individual FLAs with Verimark, the most recent of which was dated September 3, 2019. Each FLA provides for a twenty (20)-year initial term and is governed by the laws of the State of Florida, with mandatory venue for any disputes in Broward County, Florida. Under each FLA, Coastal Palms is required to pay the following fees: (i) a royalty equal to five percent (5%) of Gross Room Revenue (\"GRR\") (FLA § 4.1); (ii) a marketing-fund contribution equal to two and one-half percent (2.5%) of GRR (FLA § 4.2); and (iii) a technology fee of twelve dollars and fifty cents (\$12.50) per available room per month, adjusted annually for changes in the Consumer Price Index, with such adjustment capped at three percent (3%) per year (FLA § 4.3). Late-payment interest under the FLAs accrues at a rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month, compounded monthly (FLA § 4.6). Additionally, FLA § 15.3 provides for liquidated damages upon termination for cause in an amount equal to three times (3×) the trailing-twelve-month royalties per pr (line truncated)

**D. Mediation and Settlement.** On February 23, 2024, the Parties agreed to submit their dispute to mediation before the Honorable Patricia Everwood (Retired), of Everwood Dispute Resolution PLLC. A two-day mediation session was conducted on March 14 and 15, 2024, at 396 Alhambra Circle, Suite 800, Coral Gables, Florida 33134. A tentative settlement was reached on the second day of mediation, March 15, 2024, and the Parties executed a written term sheet memorializing the principal terms of the settlement on March 22, 2024. The Parties now desire to fully and finally resolve all claims and counterclaims in the Litigation, and all related disputes among the Parties, on the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement.

{"file_path":"response.md","content":"# Largest settlement in the firm records

## Answer

The largest settlement is **$87,500,000** in **_Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC, et al._, Case No. 1021-00006**, in the Circuit Court of the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County, Florida.

The matter concerned Verimark's claims that Coastal Palms and affiliated entities systematically underreported hotel gross-room revenue and therefore underpaid royalties, marketing-fund contributions, and technology fees under 22 franchise agreements. The settlement also resolved Coastal Palms' counterclaim and included the surrender of 14 hotel franchises, continued operation of eight properties under new franchise agreements, and security for the deferred payments.

## Why $87.5 million is the correct number

The controlling document is the **Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release (Execution Version), dated April 22, 2024**. It expressly defines:

- **“Settlement Amount”** as **$87,500,000** (Section 1.22); and
- the total settlement consideration as **$87,500,000** (Section 2.1), consisting of:
  - **$25,000,000** paid at closing; and
  - **$62,500,000** in eight semiannual structured payments of **$7,812,500** each.

The agreement separately provides for **6.5% simple interest** on the outstanding structured-payment balance. I have not added that interest to the settlement figure because the executed agreement defines the Settlement Amount as $87.5 million and treats the interest as a separate payment obligation. Likewise, I have not substituted the approximately **$150 million** in damages claimed in the complaint or the approximately **$71.2 million** value of collateral for the executed settlement amount.

The firm's closing memorandum confirms that the parties reached a tentative agreement at **$87.5 million** on March 15, 2024, that the final execution version was fully executed by all parties on April 22, 2024, that the initial $25 million was funded that day, and that the matter was closed after dismissal with prejudice on April 26, 2024.

## Matters and documents relied on

1. **`documents/matters/1021-00006/Mediation & Settlement/final-settlement-agreement-execution.docx`**
   - Title: *Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release (Execution Version)*.
   - Effective date: April 22, 2024.
   - Identifies the action as *Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC, et al.*, Case No. 1021-00006.
   - Section 1.22 defines the Settlement Amount as **$87,500,000**.
   - Section 2.1 repeats the total and specifies the $25 million upfront payment plus $62.5 million of structured payments.

2. **`documents/matters/1021-00006/Client Reporting/matter-closing-memorandum.docx`**
   - Identifies the client as Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. and the matter as the Coastal Palms franchise-revenue litigation.
   - Records the March 15, 2024 agreement at **$87.5 million**.
   - States that the final settlement agreement was fully executed on April 22, 2024, that the $25 million closing payment was funded, and that the total settlement amount was **$87.5 million**.
   - Confirms the case was dismissed with prejudice and the matter closed on April 26, 2024.

3. **`documents/matters/1021-00006/Pleadings/complaint.docx`**
   - Confirms the case caption, Case No. 1021-00006, parties, and the underlying claims.
   - Shows that the approximately **$150 million** figure was the amount claimed in litigation, not the amount fixed by the executed settlement agreement.

## Method and comparison

I screened the settlement-related materials for agreements identified as execution versions, final agreements, or mutual-release settlement agreements, and compared the monetary amount expressly fixed by each executed agreement. I excluded drafts, redlines, settlement authority memoranda, term sheets, demands, claimed damages, judgments, asset values, and transaction values that were not the settlement amount defined by the executed agreement.

As cross-checks, other large executed settlement documents in the records include a **$52.85 million** redemption price within the mutual release and settlement agreement in the Palmetto Grand Resort dispute (`documents/matters/1027-00003/Transaction Documents/mutual-release-and-settlement-agreement.docx`) and a **$47.3 million** settlement in the Hurricane Callista insurance matter (`documents/matters/1021-00003/Mediation & Settlement/settlement-agreement-mutual-release.docx`). Both are below $87.5 million.

**Conclusion:** On the firm records provided, lead with **$87.5 million — _Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC, et al._ (Case No. 1021-00006).**"}
